Some more thoughts on the disgrace of NatCon in Jerusalem.  Almost all of the conference was classic right-wing: immigration, family values, national identity, and security. On Wednesday night (Oct 7), the conference hosted a panel on the American "new right". The participants repeatedly shifted between brave truth-tellers and outsider non-experts just sharing vibes. What followed was a Groyper shitshow. 

The panelists were all unanimous that Jews need to stop speaking about antisemitism. As one speaker put it (I may be paraphrasing), charges of being a Nazi have no currency today. When challenged (by me) on whether they think that there is real antisemitism, or real Nazis, and what the response should be, they offered no answer.  

Let's be clear - antisemitism is real, and its not confined to the Left. In the past few years, there have been mass murders of Jews by neo-Nazis at the Tree of Life Synagogue in Pittsburgh (2018), the Poway Chabad Synagogue (2019). Neo-Nazis coordinated attacks on synagogues in the Northeast and Midwest in 2018. The FBI foiled plots against synagogues in Colorado in 2019. This is of course without getting into the new darlings of the right - Tucker, Fuentes, Candance Owens, Daryl Cooper. Do the panelists believe them to be antisemitic? Are we allowed to say so? They all implied that calling them out is a form of "cancel culture".  

The panelists repeated objectively false reasons for the decline in support for Israel, and not simply as descriptors. Again and again, they said (some implicitly and some more explicitly) that Israel manipulates America into costly Middle Eastern wars. This is simply a lie.  Over the past 50 years, the United States has gone to war to protect Kuwait, the Balkans, South Korea, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia and others. Americans have NEVER shed blood for Israel. Israel did not make the US conduct costly (and ultimately pointless) nation-building exercises in Iraq and Afghanistan. The recent was in Iran began when Trump promised Iranian protesters that "help is on the way". Israel, in fact, is probably America's most self-reliant and independent ally. Completely absent was any talk of American benefits to the alliance with Israel.  

Then there was the usual canard about Israel taking American money. While I am sure most conference participants would support Israel weaning itself off of American aid, let's remember that the United States wants Israel to be reliant on aid as a tool of pressuring Israel. American aid is not charity - it must be invested in American technology and weapons. It is also being progressively phased out. Jordan and Egypt also receive over a billion dollar in foreign aid packages, but I've yet to hear hostility expressed towards these countries.  

Finally, there was repeated talk of liberal Jewish American organizations, especially their support for immigration. The subtext was that Israeli Jews are somehow responsible for the policy choices of American Jews. As if there is some shadowy Jewish cabal to exploit America for Israel's sake.  The worst of all speakers was William Wolfe, who I would venture to say was the only speaker who I would characterize as an actual Jew-hater. He spoke of "Jewish" voting priorities that hurt him as an American Christian, implying that his opposition to Israel is a means of getting back at them. Let's be clear - American Jews are American citizens, and have every right to promote their political preferences. Israelis have nothing to do with that.   

Wolfe also believes that American Jews are conditional citizens. He spoke of pride of his ancestors having been in America since the Civil War, noting that no Jews signed the American constitution. So what? His implication was that they are not real or full Americans. (Somebody pointed out that Haim Solomon financed the Revolution). He also said that only one million Jews voted for Trump, out of 77 million Americans. Jews are the "junior partner" in conservatism and "need to know their place". He also spoke of his anger of American Jews largely voting Democratic. Again - so what? American Jews don't owe you anything.  

Wolfe also claimed that he wanted an American-Israeli partnership devoid of religious or cultural meaning, purely transactional. And then he took Israel to task for selling drones to Azerbaijan, which in his words kill Christians in Armenia. Of course, Azerbaijan is a close ally of Israel, and sits on Iran's border. Armenia has close ties with Iran.  

As an Orthodox Jew, its not my place to comment on Christian theology. But Wolfe took Evangelicals to task, saying that the "Old Testament" is a Christian book, for Christians, thus cutting off the Jewish roots of Christianity. In between the lines, Wolfe ascribes to classic supercessionism, in which Judaism has been replaced by Christianity and Jews have finished their historical role. That explains his antipathy to Israel and Zionism - the Jews are done and have no more right to statehood (or even existence as a group).  

Hazony and co billed this event as having hard conversations, yet they objected to partipants who had serious concerns about the points raised, vigourously denying even the possibility of antisemitism or anti-Jewish undertones. Wolfe was combatant and intentionally provocative in private exchanges. He didn't come for conversation. He came for the applause of his Groyper twitter base at telling the Joos the truth to their face.

@NatConTalk is the right wing equivalent of Jews for Mamdani, putting their prefered policy preferences ahead of Jewish security and safety. Jews were silent as the Left was taken over by antizionists and extremists, for the sake of unity against the supposed greater enemy on the Right. text:
@Treasury_RSA @GovernmentZA @SAReserveBank @_cosatu THE FACTORY SHUT AND THE AUCTION WAS SIX TIMES OVERSUBSCRIBED. IN THE SAME WEEK. SOMEONE SHOULD EXPLAIN HOW BOTH CAN BE TRUE.

Two South African numbers showed up this week, and read together, they dismantle the theory that this country's macroeconomic policy rests on.

On Tuesday, the National Treasury took R16.3 billion in bids for R2.55 billion of bonds on offer. Cover of 6.3 times, the strongest since 2 June. The 2037 alone drew R7 billion of bids against an R850 million allotment.

On Thursday,  Statistics South Africa reported that manufacturing output fell 4.3% in the year to August, and 3.1% on the month. July had been positive on both measures. Petroleum and chemicals fell 5.0%. Motor vehicles and transport equipment fell 8.8%.

So: finance queuing six deep at the Treasury window, and the factories contracting at the fastest pace in months. If you hold the orthodox framework, these two facts should be in tension. Saving is supposed to be the scarce thing. Government borrowing is supposed to compete for it, bid up its price, and squeeze private investment out. That is the crowding-out story told in every Budget Review and every ratings note about this country. Even taught at our neoliberal universities.

But there is no queue for scarce savings here. The queue is on the other side of the window. Banks, pension funds and foreign portfolios are competing to hold the liability of a state they are simultaneously told is overextended. They are not short of funds to lend. They are short of borrowers worth lending to, because the demand that would make a factory investment pay has been removed,  partly by the fuel formula, partly by a policy rate raised to 7.25% on 23 September, into a quarter in which GDP had already contracted 0.2% and gross fixed capital formation had fallen for the second consecutive time.

Let me be exact about what the auction does and does not prove, because the honest version is stronger than the triumphant one. It does not prove that borrowing is costless. The ten-year yield rose more than fifty basis points over the past month and sits above 9%.  The 2037 cleared at 9.07%. Demand was heavy at a high price. What the auction disposes of is the quantity claim — that there is a finite pool of saving which the state exhausts. There plainly is not. What remains is a price, and that price is not handed down by a scarcity of funds either. It is anchored by the repo rate the Reserve Bank sets, plus a term premium shaped by what investors expect that rate to do. The Bank administers the anchor, and then the fiscal authority treats the result as a market verdict it must obey.

This is the circularity at the centre of South African policy. The Bank raises the rate to suppress demand. Suppressed demand shows up as contracting output — manufacturing down 4.3%, investment falling, a negative quarter. Weak output weakens the revenue base. A weaker revenue base is then read as evidence that the fiscus must consolidate further to reassure the very investors who have just oversubscribed its auction six times over. Each turn of the loop is described as a discipline. Each turn makes the next turn necessary.

The instrument is pointed at the wrong thing in the first place. August's inflation was 4.4%, with food and non-alcoholic beverages at 1.1%. The pressure in the system came from imported energy: this month's fuel adjustment raised petrol 95 by R3.33 a litre while the rand moved from 16.213 to 16.212 against the dollar. The World Bank, in its regional update on Monday, projects median African inflation rising from 3.7% to 5.5% this year and attributes it to global fuel, fertiliser and food prices. A South African policy rate does not reach any of those. It reaches the bond instalment and the working-capital line of the manufacturer whose output just fell 8.8%.

The Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement is a fortnight away. The framing will be familiar: credibility, consolidation, the market's confidence to be earned. Hold it against Tuesday's auction sheet. Confidence in the sovereign's paper is not the problem. It has rarely been less of a problem. The problem is an economy with idle capacity, 570 million people on this continent without electricity, a transmission grid that needs building, and a policy framework that treats the public balance sheet as the constraint rather than the instrument.

Domestic resource creation starts from the opposite premise: that the binding limits are real: skills, energy, foreign exchange, productive capacity, and that finance follows a credible plan rather than preceding it. Tuesday's auction is the evidence. Thursday's manufacturing print is the cost of ignoring it.

The US has reportedly shelved its proposal to expand the Sudan arms embargo nationwide amid considerable opposition among UN Security Council (UNSC) members.

During a 24 August UNSC session on Sudan, the US senior advisor for African and Arab Affairs Massad Boulos pushed for the UN's pre-existing arms embargo for the Darfur region of western Sudan to be expanded worldwide.

The proposal came amid Sudanese army advances, leading analysts to suggest that it would offer a lifeline to the UAE-backed Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a militia the UN has accused of g*nocide in Sudan.

Given that the army relies on legal state defence procurement, critics warned that the US proposal would hinder Sudanese state army's ability to protect civilians.

By contrast, they warned, the UAE's illicit supply of weapons to the RSF would continue, in breach of Darfur arms embargo that has failed to stop RSF massacres in the region that UN said bore the hallmarks of g*nocide.

"The US proposal to expand the arms embargo is suspected to be driven by the UAE’s efforts to reshape Sudan’s dynamics on the ground in favour of the RSF after recent military setbacks," wrote Mutasim Ali and Yonah Ali of the Raoul Wallenberg Center for Human Rights in an article published by Just Security. 

Although the US proposal was supported by western states, Washington failed to persuade African non-permanent UNSC members to support it.

Another obstacle was pushback from veto-wielding powers China and Russia. 

Instead, the US will vote for a short-term extension of the Darfur arms embargo, which will also preserve the mandate of the independent Panel of Experts to continue tracking sanction violations and illicit weapons flow.

Nonetheless, Sudanese government advisor Amgad Fareid warned that the UAE and US are working to abolish the UN's monitoring mechanisms for Darfur altogether.

The objective must be to create an economy in which people do not merely wait for government employment but can build livelihoods through expanding private-sector opportunities.

THE COASTAL HIGHWAY: CONNECTIVITY THAT CAN UNLOCK ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY

Industrial development cannot flourish in isolation. Investors need efficient transportation networks connecting factories, ports, markets, workers and suppliers.

The proposed coastal highway connectivity forms part of a wider infrastructure vision that could improve access to Ogun's coastal communities and link economic activities along the corridor.

Better connectivity can reduce travel time and logistics bottlenecks, encourage investment and open previously underserved areas to commercial activity.

But infrastructure must be delivered responsibly, with appropriate environmental assessments, fair compensation where required, community consultation and protection of livelihoods. Development should improve the lives of residents, not make them victims of it.

A SOBERING PRECEDENT: THE NIGERIAN MARITIME UNIVERSITY CONTROVERSY

There is a historical example that makes the debate over Ogun East particularly important.

During his tenure as Minister of Transportation under President Muhammadu Buhari, Rotimi Amaechi publicly opposed continuing with the proposed Nigerian Maritime University at Okerenkoko in Delta State. In 2016, he questioned the project's priorities and cost, argued that existing maritime institutions should be strengthened first, and stated that the project should not proceed under the prevailing circumstances.

His position generated substantial controversy. Supporters of the university argued that it could develop maritime expertise, create opportunities in the Niger Delta and contribute to regional development.

The lesson is not that every proposed project must be approved regardless of cost, location, security or feasibility. Governments must scrutinise public expenditure and demand accountability.

The lesson is that a project should be judged on its merits, and legitimate concerns should lead to solutions—not the reflexive abandonment of potentially valuable investments.

If an existing institution can be strengthened while another region also receives strategic investment, why must development in one location automatically be treated as a threat to development elsewhere?

If there are concerns about cost, provide transparent figures. If feasibility is in doubt, commission independent assessments. If security is a challenge, develop a security plan. If environmental risks exist, mitigate them. If financing is inadequate, explore credible partnerships.

Do not allow a disagreement over implementation to become an excuse for denying an entire region the opportunity to develop.

Amaechi's earlier position on the maritime university is therefore relevant to the present debate as a warning against a political culture in which promising projects can become casualties of disagreements over priorities. It does not, by itself, prove what he would do in any future office, but it provides a legitimate basis for asking political leaders to explain how they would approach comparable development proposals.

THE QUESTION THE OPPOSITION MUST ANSWER

Political opposition is indispensable to democracy. No government should be above criticism, and no project should be shielded from scrutiny simply because it is associated with a particular administration.

But responsible opposition must do more than identify shortcomings. It must offer credible alternatives.

If the ADC or any other opposition party believes these Ogun East projects are misguided, let it publish its alternative development plan.

Let it explain:

- How it would attract investors and create comparable employment opportunities.

OGUN EAST MUST NOT BECOME A CASUALTY OF POLITICAL JEALOUSY: DEVELOPMENT MUST COME BEFORE PARTISAN INTERESTS!

If the opposition condemns the projects that can create jobs, attract investment and transform Ogun State, what credible alternatives are they offering the people?

The position attributed to the African Democratic Congress (ADC) on the proposed Ogun East economic development projects raises a fundamental question: Is the opposition genuinely concerned about the welfare of Ogun State, or is political competition taking precedence over the economic future of its people?

Ogun State stands at a potentially historic crossroads. The proposed Gateway Deep Sea Port, the Olokola Industrial Hub, the revival of the Olokola Liquefied Natural Gas project, the expansion of petrochemical and manufacturing activities, and improved coastal road connectivity offer an opportunity to build a new economic frontier in Ogun East.

These are not merely government publicity projects. They represent the possibility of developing an integrated maritime, energy, logistics and manufacturing ecosystem capable of generating employment, attracting domestic and foreign capital, expanding commerce and increasing government revenue.

Recent developments have strengthened the case for taking these opportunities seriously. In September 2026, the Ogun State Government announced agreements involving DP World for the Gateway Deep Sea Port and the proposed Blue Marine Special Economic Zone. Discussions with NNPC Limited have also resumed over the long-delayed Olokola LNG project. These developments are significant, although their ultimate success will depend on implementation, financing, infrastructure and sustained investor commitment.

What, then, is the alternative being offered to the people of Ogun East?

If these initiatives are rejected, delayed or abandoned for partisan reasons, what replaces the jobs, business opportunities and infrastructure they are intended to create? Where are the competing proposals for attracting investors, developing industries, empowering young people and expanding the state's productive capacity?

The people of Ogun State deserve answers—not political slogans.

THE DEEP SEAPORT: AN OPPORTUNITY TO CHANGE OGUN'S ECONOMIC DESTINY

A viable deep seaport could position Ogun State as a significant gateway for international trade, complementing existing Nigerian ports and supporting regional commerce across West Africa.

Its potential benefits extend beyond the port itself. Shipping, freight forwarding, warehousing, customs brokerage, haulage, ship-related services, manufacturing, agricultural processing and export logistics could create opportunities for businesses of different sizes.

The port could also encourage industries to establish facilities closer to shipping infrastructure, helping to reduce logistics costs and improve access to export markets.

However, these benefits are not automatic. They require reliable roads, power, water, security, transparent regulation, environmental safeguards and sustained investment. That is precisely why the project deserves serious scrutiny and responsible implementation—not reflexive political obstruction.

OLOKOLA INDUSTRIAL HUB: FROM UNTAPPED POTENTIAL TO PRODUCTIVE WEALTH

For too long, communities with substantial economic potential have watched major industrial promises remain unrealised.

The proposed Olokola industrial and maritime corridor offers an opportunity to change that trajectory. With effective planning and investment, it could support energy-intensive industries, petrochemicals, manufacturing, logistics, agro-processing and export-oriented businesses.

The revival of the Olokola LNG initiative, if successfully implemented, could further strengthen the region's energy and industrial prospects.

The greatest beneficiaries should be the people of Ogun East: young graduates seeking meaningful employment, artisans looking for customers, farmers seeking reliable markets,

text:
The Brown Envelope Republic: What Nigeria Pays Its Journalists, and What That Buys

Letters from Stockholm

By Kio Amachree

There was a time when a Nigerian editor could make a minister sweat. A front page in Lagos could end a career in Dodan Barracks. Soldiers raided newsrooms because newsrooms mattered. Dele Giwa was murdered with a parcel bomb because what he was about to print was worth killing for. The Nigerian press of the 1980s and 1990s was not perfect, but it was feared, and a press feared by the powerful is a press doing its job.

That press was not shut down by decree. It was starved. And a starving man, as every Nigerian politician knows, can be bought for the price of a meal. This week I want to put the price in numbers, in naira and in dollars, and set it beside what a reporter earns in the other English-speaking countries Nigerians like to compare themselves to.

All figures are approximate, converted at roughly 1,400 naira to the dollar, the rate the naira has been trading at this summer. Readers who remember the old rate should note that the collapse of the naira is itself part of the story.

What a Nigerian journalist is paid

Nigeria's national minimum wage is 70,000 naira a month. That is about 50 dollars. About 600 dollars a year.

Industry reporting says many working journalists earn below that floor, and graduate entrants earn far less again. Business Day has reported graduate reporters on as little as 30,000 naira a month. When that figure was first quoted it was worth around 200 dollars. Today it is worth about 21 dollars. The reporter did not get a pay cut. His country did, and his proprietor did not adjust.

Out of that sum come transport, data and airtime, because many media houses do not reimburse the cost of actually going to the story. And that is when the salary arrives at all. In 2015 the Nigeria Union of Journalists picketed ThisDay over nine months of unpaid wages. The union has issued ultimatums to owners who post profits while owing staff half a year's pay. Last year, marking its seventieth anniversary, the NUJ's national president said low pay and poor welfare are driving skilled people out of the industry. This year its FCT council warned that poor and unpaid salaries threaten the 2027 election itself. Premium Times, one of the few outlets that still pays for real investigation, has written plainly that the country's best journalists are leaving.

What the same job pays elsewhere

Britain. The NCTJ's latest Journalists at Work survey puts the average UK journalist salary at 34,500 pounds, rising to about 45,500 pounds in London. Starter reporters are on 23,000 to 26,000 pounds. Call the average 46,000 dollars a year, or about 64 million naira. A British reporter earns in roughly four working days what a Nigerian reporter on the minimum wage earns in a year.

United States. The Bureau of Labor Statistics puts the median for news analysts, reporters and journalists at 60,280 dollars a year as of May 2024. The bottom tenth of the profession, the worst-paid American reporters, are on around 34,600 dollars. That is about 84 million naira a year at the median, roughly 7 million naira a month. The worst-paid reporter in America earns in one week what a Nigerian reporter on 70,000 naira earns in a year.

Australia. Industry salary data puts the average journalist at about 64,500 Australian dollars, roughly 42,000 US dollars, or about 59 million naira.

Canada. A broadcast journalist averages around 45,000 Canadian dollars, roughly 33,000 US dollars, or about 46 million naira.

Now the African comparisons, because the excuse that "this is Africa" does not survive them.

South Africa. Salary surveys put the average journalist at about 31,000 rand a month, with entry level around 12,000 rand and senior people at 55,000 rand. The average is roughly 1,700 dollars a month, about 2.4 million naira. A mid-career South African reporter earns in one month what his Nigerian counterpart earns in nearly three years.

Kenya. WageIndicator puts the majority of Kenyan journalists between 33,000 and 118,000 shillings a month. Take the middle of that range, about 70,000 shillings, and you have roughly 540 dollars a month, about 760,000 naira. Ten times the Nigerian minimum wage, in a country with a smaller economy and no oil.

Put it on one line. Minimum wage Nigerian journalist: about 50 dollars a month. Kenyan: about 540. South African: about 1,700. Canadian: about 2,750. Australian: about 3,500. British: about 3,800. American: about 5,000. Nigeria is not at the bottom of the English-speaking world. Nigeria is a hundred times below it.

How the envelope works

A reporter is sent to cover a press conference. At the door, or afterwards in a side room, there is an envelope. Inside is cash, anything from a few thousand naira to a sum that exceeds a month's salary. The reporters call it kola, or transport, or gbalamu. The giver calls it hospitality. Both sides pretend it is not what it is.

Now do the arithmetic from the giver's side. A governor who wants a favourable front page does not need to corrupt a newspaper. He needs to find 50 dollars. For the price of one dinner in Abuja he can out-pay a reporter's employer for a month. For the price of a flight to London he can out-pay the employer for a year. Nobody in Lagos, Abuja or Port Harcourt who has ever given or received an envelope will dispute these numbers, because the numbers are the whole point.

I do not say every journalist takes it. I know men and women in Nigerian newsrooms who have refused envelopes for thirty years and paid for it in poverty and sidelining. I honour them. But Al Jazeera investigated this a decade ago and concluded that refusing was the exception, and nothing since suggests the balance has shifted.

Who built the system

The brown envelope is not a moral failure of individual reporters. It is a business model. A proprietor who pays his reporters 30,000 naira, or pays them nothing for nine months, is not running a newspaper. He is renting a platform and letting the sources pay the staff. The politician pays the journalist directly, the proprietor keeps the wage bill low, and the reader gets propaganda with a masthead on it. Everybody profits except the public.

And a remarkable number of Nigeria's outlets are owned, directly or through fronts, by sitting or former politicians, their relatives, or their business associates. A newspaper owned by a governor does not need to bribe its reporters to go easy on the governor. It simply does not pay them enough to go anywhere else.

What the muzzle costs

A country where reporters cannot afford to spend three months on a story is a country where no one audits the Lagos-Calabar highway contract, no one chases the asset declarations that have never been published, no one follows the money to Gibraltar and Paris and St John's Wood. The diaspora has been forced into the role that Lagos newsrooms used to fill, from Stockholm and London and Houston, with no budget and no access, because the people with the access have been priced out of asking.

The powerful no longer need to jail journalists, though they still do. The Committee to Protect Journalists counted ninety-one journalists arrested or detained in Nigeria in a single year under this administration. But detention is a blunt tool. Poverty is a scalpel. A reporter on 21 dollars a month with a sick mother does not need to be threatened. He needs only to be offered.

And the best people have simply gone. Into public relations, where the bank pays on the twenty-fifth of every month. Into the civil service. Into the same ministries they used to cover. Into London and Toronto with the rest of the japa generation, where the same skills are worth sixty times more. The young graduate who would have been the next Dele Giwa is writing press releases, because press releases pay.

What the Kio Solution demands

I have called before for a Dele Giwa Law to protect journalists from politically ordered arrest and torture. That law is still needed. But a journalist protected from the DSS and abandoned to hunger is not free. So I add the following.

First, a statutory minimum wage for journalists, set at a multiple of the national minimum and indexed to inflation, enforced by the National Industrial Court, with proprietors personally liable for arrears. The NUJ has talked about a bill against unpaid salaries for years. Pass it.

Second, mandatory publication of beneficial ownership for every licensed newspaper, radio and television station in Nigeria. The public has a right to know which politician owns the paper they are reading.

Third, a ban on cash payments to journalists by government ministries, agencies and state houses, with every media engagement budget published line by line. If a governor wants coverage, let him earn it.

Fourth, a public interest journalism fund, financed by a levy on political advertising and administered by an independent board with no serving politician on it, to pay for the long investigations no commercial outlet in Nigeria can now afford.

Fifth, the Isabel Precedent applied to media corruption: where a proprietor is found to have received state funds to shape coverage, the licence is suspended and the funds recovered.

A note on what this is not

This is not an attack on Nigerian journalists. I have spent my life around newsrooms and I know what it costs to tell the truth in Lagos. It is an attack on a system designed to make honesty unaffordable, and on the men who designed it. Nothing I write is personal. It is politics.

A nation gets the press it pays for. Kenya pays ten times what Nigeria pays and gets a press that can still embarrass a president. Britain pays seventy times and gets a press that brought down a Prime Minister over a birthday cake. Nigeria pays 50 dollars a month and gets a chorus of praise singers with press cards. Until the reporter can live on his salary, the envelope will keep doing the talking, and the people who stuff it will keep running the country.

Nigeria belongs to Nigerians.

#BrownEnvelope #NigerianPress #DeleGiwaLaw #PressFreedom #NUJ #JournalistsPay #NigeriaShameOnYou #DiasporaVoice #TheKioSolution #LettersFromStockholm #KioAmachree

These elements are all uniformly mixed throughout the star. The star "enters" the main sequence when its core reaches a temperature (several million kelvins) high enough to begin fusing hydrogen-1 (the predominant isotope), and establishes hydrostatic equilibrium. (In astrophysics, stellar fusion is often referred to as "burning", with hydrogen fusion sometimes termed "hydrogen burning".) Over its main sequence life, the star slowly fuses the hydrogen in the core into helium; its main-sequence life ends when nearly all the hydrogen in the core has been fused. Latin Origin: It derives from rubeus (red or reddish, like a blackberry before it ripens).
Shift in Spanish: Over time in Spanish, the meaning shifted from "red" to describe golden, yellowish, or fair hair and complexions (blond). It historically started as a nickname for someone with red hair, a red beard, or a ruddy complexion before generalizing to fair-haired individuals.

These elements are all uniformly mixed throughout the star. The star "enters" the main sequence when its core reaches a temperature (several million kelvins) high enough to begin fusing hydrogen-1 (the predominant isotope), and establishes hydrostatic equilibrium. (In astrophysics, stellar fusion is often referred to as "burning", with hydrogen fusion sometimes termed "hydrogen burning".) Over its main sequence life, the star slowly fuses the hydrogen in the core into helium; its main-sequence life ends when nearly all the hydrogen in the core has been fused. For the Sun, the main-sequence lifetime is approximately 10 billion years. More massive stars burn their fuel disproportionately faster and so have a shorter lifetime than less massive stars.

text:
First Sunday in October  Our Lady of the Most Holy Rosary of Manaoag, Pangasinan, Philippines.
.
In the 1600s, not long after many natives converted to Catholicism, word spread that a Pangasinan man coming home from his farm had seen the Virgin. As night fell, the man saw a light on a hill; drawing nearer, he saw the radiant form of a mother holding her infant standing in a tree. She called him by name, then said, “Son, I want a church here in my honor. My children shall receive many favors in this place.” Although the local priest discounted the man's story, pilgrims began coming and miracles occurring. A surge of grassroots devotion organized around a bamboo chapel at the apparition site, containing a Spanish ivory statue brought in 1605 by Dominican missionary Juan de San Jacinto. The place began to be known as Manaoag, from "mantatawag," the call. Around 1670, Dominican pastor Diego de Ballesteros built a new church for the image near the old mission chapel of Santa Monica on the Baloquin River. But on the day the statue was to be transferred, the new building had vanished without a trace. Everyone, including the skeptical clergy, decided this meant Heaven was serious about the desired location of Our Lady's church. In 1710, some Spanish benefactors, Gaspar Gamboa and his wife Agatha Yangta, funded construction of a magnificent church at the apparition site, officially donated to the Dominicans in 1733 and dedicated to Nuestra Señora del Santissimo Rosario. A hundred years later, a series of earthquakes ruined the structure, but the statue survived and continued to receive pilgrims in the rubble. In the late 1800s, work began on a new church, almost completed when the Philippine Revolution broke out against the Spanish. Both the priests and the Virgin went into hiding; rebels looted and burned the shrine. When the Dominicans returned in 1901, they found a lone saint, Fr. Mariano Pacis, tending to the spiritual life of Manaoag. By 1920, they had rebuilt the church. Msgr. Guillermo Piani, Apostolic Delegate of the Philippines, crowned the statue on April 21, 1926. Pilgrims continue to flock to the shrine, for Saturday blessing of vehicles, fiestas on the third Wednesday after Easter and the first Sunday of October, and for help throughout the year from the patron of the sick, needy, and helpless and the province of Pangasinan.
.
Timeline:
.
1610
.
According to tradition, a middle aged farmer was on his way from a grueling day in his farm. Foremost in his mind, of course, was his family. He worried about his home and his crops which he knew would be laid to waste any time the raiders come for another depredation. Faced with this hopeless prospect, he resorted to the wellsprings of his faith. He has been taught by the good Padre to have full trust and faith in the goodness and mercy of God and in the protection offered by the Heavenly Mother. These thought came into him. He signed resignedly to Virgin Mary and somehow his fears vanished as he continued his slow homeward. As he followed the path from the hill in the deepening dusk, he became aware of a mysterious light coming from somewhere. He turned to the west to assure himself that he was not being deceived, and sure enough he saw that the sun has set. He made a full and turned his gaze to the light- a tree nearby. Instantly he recognized the radiant face of a woman holding an infant in her arms. Unable to grasp that significant of the phenomenon and overcome by superstition, he wanted to run. In a moment of hesitation, he heard a sweet voice called out his name. He stood transfixed at the smiling face of the mysterious Lady. He kept down, she continued in her singularly sweet voice. "Son, I want a church built here in my honor. My children shall receive many favors in this place."
.
Overflowing with joy in that extraordinary experience, the man told his tale to his wife, children, relatives and friends. But when he went to tell it to the parish priest he got a different reception. The old Padre not only did not believe him but went on to insinuate that the man was suffering from hallucination that was induced by the extreme heat of the day.
.
Nevertheless, the story spread far and wide. People in the neighboring settlements heard of it and they came to see for themselves. These pilgrims went home not only assured of the truth of the event but but also felt that their petitions had been answered. The pilgrimage to the Lady developed into a least once a year event to fulfill a vow, make new petition to her, and offer their devotion to her.
.
Coming home from their visit to the place of the Lady's appearance and on being asked along the way from where they came, the early pilgrims would point to the general directions of the settlement and answer “ Dimad Apo ya Mantataoa ”, or from the Lady who Calls. In time the rest of the words in the phrase were dropped and a derivation was substituted - MANAOAG. This remained the name of the town.
.
A crude chapel made of light materials and nipa was erected on the spot where the Virgin is said to have appeared. On its altar was placed the Spanish statue of our Lady of the Holy Rosary which Fr. Juan de San Jacinto brought from Mexico.
.
In order to give the Virgin a more fitting house for veneration, a large wooden church was erected by Fr. Diego de Ballesteros side by side with the original mission chapel of Santa Monica in Baloquin river. The construction was meticulously supervised by the same priest who originally believed that the alleged vision of the rural folk was merely the product of the tropical heat.
.
1669 or 1670
.
When the new church was completed and the transfer of the image was set, a mysterious incident happened. In the morning of that day a large crowed assembled by the nipa chapel to accompany the Lady to her home. But the devout congregation was dumbfounded when some people rushed in shouting that the new church had disappeared. The priest and some of the people rushed to verify the news and could not find any trace of the church on the site. The people gave countless interpretations of the mystery, but everybody agreed that the Lady did not want her throne at any other place except at the spot she indicated, in her appearance several decades ago.
.
The enthusiasm of the inhabitants and the pilgrims became even more ardent after the disappearance of the Baloquin church. Everyone was more convinced that the vision was true, that it was divine land and more could hinder it. Hence, plans were laid out to build a larger and stronger church made of bricks to replace the small rundown chapel.
.
1701
.
A very devout Spanish caballero and member of the Dominican Third Order, Don Gaspar Gamboa and his wife Dona Agatha Yangta promised to shoulder whatever cost the construction would incur. In the same year, the construction was started. Many laborers were hired but there were others who volunteered their services. As others baked clay for the bricks, others would carry the finished materials to the construction site where they were placed on the planned area. After many days of work, it became a magnificent edifice. The natives and especially the pilgrims were delighted at the new home of the Blessed Mother.
.
The façade of the church gaped with three big doors. Above each of these were three huge wooden windows that gave enough light and color to the choir left. To the left, a soaring cylindrical tower of monumental beauty was built, of solid stones.
.
Simultaneously with the construction of the new church, Don Gaspar built a big chapel of bricks near the Baloquin river. This was not to replace the church that mysteriously disappeared, but as a place for the image since all penitential processions of the pilgrims traditionally started from this point. Not a trace of this church can be found today; each stone and brick has been carried away by pilgrims who treasured relics and souvenirs of this visit to the ever watchful Virgin of Manaoag.
.
1722
.
Don Gaspar, the chief patron of new church, signed the perpetual document turning over the edifice and the Baloquin chapel to the Dominican Province of the Holy Rosary.
.
1739
.
Having taken possession and care of the sanctuary church, the Dominican fathers started renovating the interior. Rosary images were installed to enhance the splendor of the interior, and a thick wall was built to the divide the nave in order to give room to a spacious sacristy. The remodeling took 30 years to finish but the real artistic touch was yet to follow.
.
.
1777
Huge columns were erected at the sides of the chapel of Our Lady. Each one supported a medallion representing each one of the 15 mysteries of the Rosary. Also, in addition that year, the Lady was enthroned in a case gilded with solid silver.
.
1832
.
Four successive earthquakes so weakened the structure and it crumbled to pieces. After that catastrophe, a makeshift shelter inside the remaining walls was built for our Lady so the congregation and pilgrims could continue their devotions to her and they despite the inconveniences.
.
1840
.
No immediate effort was made to rebuild the church, instead a huge bell weighing 2,000 kilos was purchased.
.
1880
.
The parish priest made a study of materials and they decided that corrugated galvanized iron was a better roof than tiles. But hardly had the roof been placed, when together intense earthquake struck and damage the church. The soaring tower cracked from the top bottom and was condemned as hazard. It was manually torn down and its bells were lowered down. For a long period of time the bells stayed under the trees behind the church, exposed to the elements.
.
1882
.
Fr. Hilario del Campo commenced the restoration of damage portions of the church. Wanting to make sturdier and larger structure, he made deep drilling at the transepts ad filled these with concrete. The four huge columns that support the dome of the present church rest on the 10-meter foundation which he laid. Repair and restoring work had gone for a decade and was nearing completion when every new addition buckled down.
.
To provide shelter for Our Lady of the Rosary and a repository of the sacred vessels including the silver altar, a small bamboo chapel was built at the site of the church by making use of the old rubbles. Huge reinforcing columns, 3 meters in diameter were built to reinforce the walls.
.
1896
.
When the wings and roofing were blowing, the thick walls were already standing and roofing it has started. The work, however, was badly hampered by the revolution. The priests hid themselves from the insurgents and the laborers were outlawed.
.
Inevitably, the Spanish priests were captured and brought to Manila as detainees. But before that, Fr. Jose Puente, O.P. was able to smuggle to image of our Lady from Manaoag to Dagupan for safekeeping.
.
The flight of the image from Manaoag to Dagupan was no less heroic than the earlier trials. Fr. Puente knew that this attempts, cannot be kept secret from the people and that the sooner or later the insurgents would know about it. He was sure that there as an attempt to capture the image and him with it. He also knew that he could rely on no one except on his faith in the Divine Providence.
He loaded the image in a carabao-cart and started for Dagupan. On the way, simple peasant men volunteered to accompany him. Armed with bolos, fought the insurgents who staged an ambush. Not a few of them sacrificed their lives in that battle.
.
Finally, the Lady reached Dagupan as if in exile. She took shelter in Dagupan Church. Every now and then news would leak that the insurgents would ransack the church and divest it of its precious ornaments and sacred vessels. But every time these plots became known, pious laymen, especially the Dominican teriaries would secretly bring the image to their homes. Here, the Lady who is the refuge of sinners became a refugee from sinners.
.
May 10, 1898
.
The ravaging insurgents ransacked the makeshift chapel in Manaoag and divested it of the treasures that were still housed there. After having looted the church of its valuables, the insurgents burned it down.
.
Looting of the churches was the order of the day during this period. the insurgents were in bad need of metals to cast the cannons, firearms and ammunitions. Even the vicar general of Vigan Fr. Gregorio Aglipay, made several circular letters admonishing and ordering Catholic Parish priest to hand over to the military at the Jefature in Dagupan the much needed metals from their churches ”for the sake of God and country.”
.
The Philippines church suffered a lot during the Filipino-Spanish American War. Parochial churches in Pangasinan that were manned by Spanish Dominicans were left without shepherds. A wave of nationalism brought about demands that these churches be turned over to Filipino clergy.
.
During those bad times, an exemplary and saintly priest came to the succor of the abandoned flock in Manaoag, he was Fr. Mariano Pacis. He built a small convent and a bible chaper where the scattered flock could gather to fulfill their religious obligations and to pray for better times. It was probably because of this that Manaoag was saved from holocaust of the insurrection.
.
The war ended with the Treaty of Paris. The Spanish priests were again permitted to return to their former post. But with all the raging agitation for the Filipination of Parishers, the Spanish Dominicans refused to return to Pangasinan. However, the Bishop of Nueva Segovia, initiated there return at least to their first establishment in Pangasinan. Finally they accede to the pleas of high ecclesiastical authority, but instead of Binalatongan (now San Carlos City ) they chose the Sanctuary of Manaoag which was donated to the province of the Holy Rosary with inalienable rights.
.
1901
.
The Dominican Provincial sent there priest to Manaoag, namely; Fr. Cipriano Pampliegs, Mariano Revilla and Jose Bartolo. They were delighted to find Fr. Pacis in his small convent. Since they could not as yet stay in the old convent because it was occupied by the members of the American Armed Forces, the four priests stayed together in Fr. Pacis’ convent-hut.
.
January 16, 1902
.
After the Americans moved out, the priests were not able to settle in their own house.
.
Times were bleak and uncertain for the priest. The hangover of anti-Spanish feelings was still around. But for them, a mission has to be done, in particular to care for the Sanctuary of Our Lady. So as soon as they had settled down they set out to roof the unfinished church. But at the outset, they left the wings of the transepts untouched because of financial difficulties. The covering of the whole church was finally finished in 1906, although much remained to be down in the interior.
.
Improvement of the interior of the church continued. Every day after mass, sharp at tatto chirpings of chisels and hammer filled the interior of the church as workmen etched on the intricate design of the main altar, the niche and the throne of the Blessed Virgin. In 1909 when the church was again fit to be the home of the Heavenly Mother, its image in Dagupan was brought home and enthroned in her own shrine.
.
1911
.
All major works on the church were completed between the years 1911 and 1920 except the belfry and the wings of the transports. The restoration of the Blessed Virgin to her original home in the Sanctuary Church however brought in more devotees and pilgrims. In gratitude for favors received they poured in their hard-earned centavos and niches. In this manner, funds were raised to purchase a nickel-plated carriage plated on which her image during processions. This also enables the Dominican Father to finish the work on the colossal dome in 1913. It was in this manner that devotees of May, the Lady of the Most Holy Rosary who themselves built the present church. As it stands today, it measures 89 meters long and 13.5 meters wide. The transept measures 53.50 meters long and 15.10 meters wide. The dome is 35 meters high. The belfry is 40 meters high.
.
1937
.
The Sanctuary Church of Manaoag was awarded the Merit of Recognition by the Philippines Historical Research and Makers Committee through its Chairman Walter Robb and Fr. Miguel Selga, S.J. the historical marker was affixed to the church’s wall near the main door in March that year. The marker reads:
.
“Administration since 1605 by the Dominicans, the first church of wood lasted a century. The second one which was of stone was built through the generosity of Gaspar and Agatha, and inaugurated in 1720. In 1733 it was donated to the Dominican Corporation, but was destroyed by the earthquake of 1892. The Provincial church, built of wood, was burned during the insurrection of 1898. The reconstruction of the present church began in 1991 with the return of the Dominicans."
.
April 21, 1926
.
The image of the Nuestra Señora de Manaoag, famous throughout Pangasinan, was preserved in Dagupan during the revolution, and then taken back to the Sanctuary by the people of Manaoag where it was solemnly crowned in the presence of thousands of faithful, by Mons, Guillermo Piani, Apostolic Delegate to the Philippines.
April 14, 1937
.
The plaque was solemnly unveiled by the member of the committees of the Historical Commission with the customary church pageantry. The main speech was delivered by the Bishop of Pangasinan, Msgr. Cesar Guerrero and the response was given by Fr. Basilio Martin, O.P. curator of the Sanctuary. That day also coincided with the traditional fiesta of Our Lady hence a huge crowd witnessed the occasion.
.
The Japanese invasion and subsequent occupation of the country during the WW II did not spare the Sanctuary church from ravages of war. During the initial stages the priests themselves went in hiding and so, for the time, the church was closed. When fighting stopped and an uncertain place returned, the church was once more. However, due to the difficulty of travel and restriction imposed on the movement of the people by the occupation forces, pilgrimages stopped. The priests came out from hiding and performed services for the few dared attend services.
.
It was during the liberation period that the church suffered slight damages. Gen. Mc Arthur’s forces landed in nearby San Fabian and from there, they conducted an intense bombing and bombardment of big buildings in the surrounding towns which were suspected housing enemy troops. Eyewitnesses recall how one plane dropped four bombs intended for the church. One cell through the church’s roof but did not explode. In that trial, a religious brother was killed. He was rushing to the church to secure the Image of the Virgin when the bombs fell and exploded.
.
The end of the war ushered peace and prosperity. The church was repaired and scars of war were patched up. The pilgrims returned in even greater numbers, presumably to see their Blessed Mother again, and to offer prayers of the thanksgiving for having been spared. For those who suffered misfortunes, they came to seek consolation from the “CALLING VIRGIN. ”
.
Immediately after the liberation, a school was opened beside the church to cater to the youth who have been shut off from school during the war. In no time, the school population exerted pressure on the convent. They crowded the corridors and halls. It soon became apparent that a new residence for the priest was needed.
.
1952
.
Work started on the convent and the belfry. In 2 years both structures were finished and in 1954, the Marian Year, they were inaugurated.
.
May 1973
.
The church again suffered minor misfortune. Times were hard and there was great demand for antiques. These motivated the person or persons who might have robbed the Blessed Lady of her Golden Crown and her pendant cross. The crown which has never been recovered was ages-old and the pendant cross used to be pectoral cross of the bishop-saint of Vietnam and the blessed Geronimo Hermosilla. The crown has since been replaced through generous donation of the faithful.
.
1972
.
Today, the sanctuary-Church is under the administration and care of Filipino Dominicans. It was turned over to Rev. Fr. Crispin Marqueses, O.P. as the first prior. He, however, did not stay long in his post due to illness. A year after he was replaced by Rev. Reynaldo Adalid, O.P.
.
Since the assumption to the office, Fr. Adalid has introduced many improvements with an eye for aesthetic beauty. He replaced the rotten wooden platform of the Sanctuary with an octagonal granolithic marble dais. Decorative electric chandeliers were hung above the presbytery. He also installed and excellent sound system to suit the church’s acoustics. This enhances better communications with the faithful on the word of God during the mass.
.
Other important additions are the Yamaha organ, a bamboo symphony and a home for the boys who serve as choir of the church. The old pipe organ also been repaired. As of this date, the rotting ceiling above the altar has been replaced and painted.
The interior, the façade and the belfry have been given a new coat of paint. A civic action team of the Philippine Air Force (PAF) is doing the face-lifting, courtesy of General Jose Racundo, in close coordination with Gen. Abraham Mangonon, General Abaya and Major Iglesias. Materials are purchased from cash donations of devotees and patrons of the Manaoag Virgin and her Shrine.

text:
Fair challenge, but I think you’re looking for those values in the wrong place, they don’t live online. They’re in jury rooms, parish halls, Scout and Cub groups, Sunday league touchlines, allotment societies, bell-ringing bands, pub quiz teams and PTAs. Orwell said we were a nation of stamp-collectors, pigeon-fanciers and darts-players. He was describing our English liberty: private, voluntary life organised by the people who do it, not mandated by the state.

That’s where the values are, you turn up when it’s raining, turn up for the people relying on you, and stay involved in your community, whatever that may be.

Several items on your “European” list are as English as anything. Orwell named respect for the law as something above the state in 1941. I won’t mourn deference to class hierarchy, though.

Where I agree is that it’s disappearing. Volunteering has been falling for a decade. The state’s has tried to gut it out of us, all they gave us (and the people who came here) was four values lifted from a counter-terror strategy, plus a quiz. Civic nationalism is never going to work here because it offers nothing to join. They told everyone there was nothing to join.

We have to keep these institutions, societies and communities alive. There’s demand for them: grassroots football is thriving and the Scouts and Cubs have waiting lists. It just doesn’t look like it from on here.

text:
Great American Fishing — Description and Synopsis

*Written 25 September 2026; updated 30 September 2026. Describes the game as it stands in the
official build (Official0926) plus everything on the NEW TEST build since: the AI anglers on eight
lakes, the licensed soundtrack, the new characters and the Copper Bass Boat.*

---

## Synopsis

**Great American Fishing** is a realistic, relaxed freshwater fishing game set across ten American
lakes, from cold northern waters and a snow-capped crescent lake to a warm cypress swamp, a wooded
South Carolina reservoir and a red-rock desert reservoir. You are not alone on the water: on most
lakes other anglers work the banks around you, casting, fighting and landing their own fish. You fish
from the bank, the dock or your own boat, reading the water, the weather and the time of day to find
fish, then choosing the right rod, reel, line, rig and lure to fool them.

Every fish in the lake is simulated. Each one has a home, a depth it likes, a mood that changes with
the season, the weather and the light, and its own reaction to your lure: it may ignore it, follow it,
nose up to it, or strike. Once hooked, its size, strength and stamina decide the fight, and your line
can break or be bitten through.

Between trips you return to a lodge: a fishing journal of every catch, a tackle shop, trophy mounts
of your best fish, photos of your catches, awards, and an aquarium where the fish you kept swim in a
wooden tank. Bass anglers can enter tournaments and work through a career season from Weekend Angler
to Champion. Each lake hides one legendary giant.

The tone is calm and warm: acoustic country and Americana music on the menus, a soft guitar at dawn
and sunset, quiet while you fish in the middle of the day, lake ambience, birds at dawn, frogs at
dusk, and the quiet satisfaction of a good fish in the hand.

---

## The world

### Ten lakes
| Lake | Character |
|---|---|
| Pine Lake | The home lake: timbered coves, a plank pier and the first fish most players meet |
| Hollow Creek | A creek-fed lake with dense grass and shoreline cover |
| Dunn Lake | A mid-sized lake with channels and open shelves |
| Top Water Lake | Shallow, weedy water made for surface lures |
| Cypress Fork | A warm three-fork swamp lake among cypress trees |
| Arrow Point | A cold crescent lake under snowy mountain peaks |
| Big Lake | A 1.6 km lake with deep basins, islands, mountains and a long pier |
| Pine Ridge | A 5.6 m-deep pond on a flat plain with a pier |
| Red Mesa Lake | A horseshoe desert reservoir with flooded timber and mesas |
| Lake Greenwood | A warm South Carolina reservoir winding through wooded hills, with finger coves, two islands and drowned timber |

Each lake has its own water temperature, and that decides which species live there. Lakes are dressed
with real lakebed habitat: weeds, logs, stumps, brush piles and boulders, which fish use as cover.
Every shoreline has giant reeds and patches of wildflowers (poppies, daisies, yellow and purple).

### Other anglers *(new)*
There is no multiplayer, so the lakes are shared with computer anglers instead: **16 of them on
eight lakes**, fishing from the bank.

| Lake | Anglers |
|---|---|
| Red Mesa | 2: the left bank near the dock, and across the bay |
| Pine Lake | 1, just left of the pier |
| Dunn Lake | 2, on the far banks |
| Top Water | 2 |
| Cypress Fork | 2, one either side of you |
| Big Lake | 2, along the shore from the pier |
| Pine Ridge | 2: on the raised bank, and across the pond |
| Lake Greenwood | 3 |

- Each one casts, works the lure back with the odd twitch, and now and then hooks a bass: the rod
  bends, the fish runs, thrashes and jumps, and he lands it and lets it go, or loses it.
- You can hear them: the lure plops in, the reel spins, the fish splashes, and sometimes they call out
  when they land one. It fades with distance.
- They stand in the same spots every visit, wear different outfits from yours, and you can't walk
  through them.
- Hollow Creek and Arrow Point have none yet: their shorelines are due to be reshaped first.
- Planned: anglers in boats, anglers you can talk to for tips, and tournament rivals on the water.

### Time, weather and seasons
- A 24-hour clock (about 40 minutes of play for a full day): sunrise, midday, sunset, a moonlit night
  with stars, dawn mist and amber evening haze.
- Weather: clear, overcast, rain and storm, with raindrop rings, lightning and thunder. Fish bite
  better under cloud and in light rain.
- Seasons follow the real calendar: spring brings fish shallow, summer middays and winter push them deep.

### Wildlife and sound
- Frogs and turtles swim, surface and dive.
- Each lake has its own ambience (desert wind at Red Mesa, morning mist at Arrow Point) plus birds by
  day and an evening chorus.
- Catch voices on big fish ("Oh yeah", "Get her done").

### Music *(new: licensed soundtrack)*
Eleven tracks, each tied to a place or a moment, crossfading as you move between them:

| Where | Track |
|---|---|
| Main menu | Country Background – Acoustic Fields (Sonican) |
| Lake selection | Lake Fishing – Inspirational Acoustic Guitars (Dream-Protocol) |
| Tackle shop and tackle box | Country – Countryside (Folk_Tales) |
| Fishing journal | Florist (TAD) |
| Trophy lodge | A Small Fire Will Do (Cal McEachern) |
| Pause menu at a lake | Forest Ambience (TinyWorlds) |
| On the lake at dawn, until 8:30 am | Etirwer (Kistol) |
| On the lake from 5:30 pm to dark | Sunset Plains (Yoiyami) |
| On the lake at night | Exploration Theme (Cleyton Kauffman) |
| Rain in the morning / afternoon | Morning Rain / Rainy Forest (TAD) |

Clear midday fishing and thunderstorms are quiet on purpose: the lake is the soundtrack. Music on the
lake plays softly under the ambience. A tension layer builds under a fish fight, and a short swell
plays when you land one. Every artist is on the in-game Credits page and in CREDITS.md.

---

## The fish

- **27 species**: largemouth, smallmouth, spotted, Alabama, shoal, Guadalupe, redeye and Florida bass;
  bluegill, black crappie and yellow perch; rainbow, brown, brook and lake trout; salmon and chum
  salmon; northern pike, walleye, sauger, catfish, carp, lake sturgeon, alligator gar, bowfin and
  paddlefish; plus whitefish. All 27 are in the journal, each with a portrait.
- **Every fish is simulated**, not rolled: it roams from a home spot, holds at its own depth, and
  judges your lure by its speed, depth and type. Some lures must be kept moving; a paused lure still
  gets a strike from a fish that saw it working.
- **Fish you can see**: animated models that swim, hover, burst, follow the lure, mouth it, shake their
  heads when hooked, leap, and gasp when landed. Species with a jaw open it as they strike, and a
  chasing fish glides smoothly behind the lure.
- **Sizes are real**: the fish you see is the fish you fight. Size classes at the landing
  (Small, Average, BIG ONE!, HUGE!) and an "A BIG ONE'S CLOSE BY!" warning.
- **Legends**: one named giant per lake, feeding only in her own windows, with a harder fight and a
  place on the lodge wall.
- **Deep water is alive**: fish hold through the whole water column, not just the top two metres.

---

## Fishing

### Casting and the retrieve
- Charge and release to cast, with an on-water target reticle that shows where the lure will land.
  Short, medium and long casts each have their own throwing motion (light flick, full cast, big heave).
- Retrieve speeds, a twitch (T / middle mouse / X on a pad) that excites a following fish, and a
  chase camera that drops underwater when a fish follows your lure.
- Topwater blow-ups: bass, pike and trout explode through surface lures, half the time in slow motion.

### The fight
- Tension, drag and line strength decide it. Hookset timing matters. Fish dive early, run, jump and
  tire. A tension gauge and a fight panel on the right keep the middle of the screen clear.
- FISH! / MISS! callouts on the hookset.
- Slack line looks slack, the angler leans into a fish's runs, and the fight camera comes up to the
  surface near the dock. Lures and fish leave ripples out to the full 40 m cast.

### Tackle
- **Rods**: several rods with their own blanks and actions, which bend properly under load.
- **Reels**: four reels changing wind speed, line strain and drag strength.
- **Line**: 6, 10 and 16 lb.
- **Lures and bait**: more than 35, each with its own swimming action: crankbaits, jerkbaits,
  swimbaits, spinnerbaits with spinning blades, jigs, soft plastics, poppers, a hollow-body frog,
  spoons and a live nightcrawler (+15% bites).
- **Rig building**: leaders (fluorocarbon, or wire so pike cannot bite you off), hook sizes, sinkers,
  leader length, and a pencil float whose depth you set (+/-) that really holds the bait.
- **Hooks and sinkers** *(new)*: small, medium and large hooks, split shot and bullet weights, sold
  in their own shop tab. The sinker you choose is drawn on the line (split shot above the lure, a
  bullet weight on its nose for a Texas rig), and Tackle Setup offers only what you own.
- **Tackle shop** with product art for every item, and saved tackle setups.

### Landing a fish
- Your angler holds the catch: big fish level across the chest, small fish cupped in both hands.
- A catch screen with species, weight, length, lake, lure, method and time, and three choices:
  **Keep Fish**, **Release Fish** or **View in Log**.
- Every catch is photographed and priced in dollars.

---

## Boats

Six boats, each with its own seat position, handling and camera:

| Boat | Notes |
|---|---|
| Bass Boat | The classic navy bass boat with a live sonar screen |
| Sport Cruiser | A larger cruiser |
| Aluminium Boat | A small utility jon boat in the fleet's navy, red and white livery, with a bright aluminium gunwale and navy/white pedestal seats |
| Graphite Bass Boat | The black high-performance boat: about 4.5x faster, a crisp red-and-white sheer stripe with GREAT AMERICAN FISHING lettering, a modelled helm with a turning wheel, a matching passenger console with glovebox and grab rail, and a bow trolling motor that deploys, spins and steers |
| Gold Cruiser | Gold hull, steering wheel that turns with the driver's hands, spinning twin propellers, its own sonar |
| Copper Bass Boat | Navy metal flake with silver swooshes and copper pinstripes, the Great American Fishing logo on a V8 outboard, live sonar. Its hardware moves: the outboard steers with the wheel and tilts up while the trolling motor is down, the trolling motor twists and swings down into the water, and two power poles come down when you drop the anchor. As fast as the Graphite |

- Every angler sits at the wheel properly on every boat: the seat slides and the body leans to reach, whatever the arm length.
- Drive from the helm, then walk to the bow to cast. Anchor, trolling mode (U), and two boat cameras (V).
- Live sonar shows depth history and fish echoes.
- A wake on the water and hull wash in the sound.

---

## Your angler

Thirteen anglers to choose from (the Handyman comes in four outfits), including the Survivalist
(default), the Tactical Sentinel, Big Kevin, the Ranger, the Fighter and, since 29 Sept, Tasha, Cole and
Reese. First-person and third-person views, with hands placed properly on rod and reel, a cast wind-up,
and the rod carried while jogging. In a fight you can work the rod hard left, right, up and down, and
the hands stay on it on every character with fingers (Big Kevin has none, on purpose).

---

## Getting started *(new)*

- **First-time tutorial**: six steps for a new angler's first catch (look, cast, reel, set the hook,
  fight, land), each finished by doing it. Only new saves see it; Backspace skips it.
- **Main menu** in the navy, cream and gold style (Version 0.75).
- **Display setting**: windowed sizes that fit your screen, borderless or fullscreen.

---

## Progress and the lodge

- **Profiles**: separate save profiles; your journal, collection and tournaments follow the profile.
- **Fishing journal (J)**: every catch with field notes, personal bests and statistics per species.
- **Money**: catches earn dollars (real tackle prices, sponsor-style payouts per pound); spend them in
  the shop.
- **Trophy lodge (L)**:
  - **Mounts**: six display slots for your personal bests
  - **Photos**: your latest catch photos
  - **Awards**: achievements and the Legends of the Lakes
  - **Milestones**: long-term goals
  - **Aquarium** *(new)*: the fish you kept swim in a warm-lit wooden tank with sand, rocks, plants,
    a sunken log and bubbles. Choose a fish with Up/Down, release it with X.
- **Live well** *(new)*: Keep Fish puts a catch in your live well (5 fish). When it is full, keeping
  a bigger fish culls your smallest, like a tournament bag. Leaving the lake moves them to the aquarium
  (12 fish).

---

## Competition

- **Bass tournaments**: a 10-minute day, black bass over 12 inches, a five-fish bag with culling,
  19 computer anglers, places, a weigh-in and your best finish per lake. Top five are paid into your
  wallet ($60 / $35 / $20 / $10 / $10).
- **Career**: a season of tournaments, one per bass lake, with a championship at Red Mesa. The field
  gets tougher each event; points and ranks run from Weekend Angler to Champion.
- **Daily challenge**: a lake and a species each day, with bronze, silver and gold, and a streak.

---

## Controls (keyboard; pad equivalents in the game)

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Left mouse | Cast (hold to charge) / set the hook / reel |
| Right mouse | Cancel cast / release fish |
| T or middle mouse | Twitch the lure |
| Enter / F / J | Keep / Release / View in Log on the catch screen |
| B | Switch lure |
| K | Tackle |
| J | Journal |
| L | Trophy lodge |
| E | Board / leave the boat |
| C | Driver's seat / bow |
| N | Sonar |
| U | Trolling motor |
| X | Anchor (the Copper Bass Boat's power poles come down with it) |
| V | Boat camera |
| Tab | Camera view |
| Z | Float camera |
| + / - | Float depth |
| Esc | Pause menu (tournaments, settings, travel) |

---

## Technical

- Unreal Engine 5.8, DirectX 11 / Shader Model 5, no Nanite or Lumen, built to run on modest hardware.
- Every lake's ground is a Landscape.
- Holds 60 fps on Big Lake on the development PC; the old periodic stutter (the sonar) is fixed.
- Saves are protected: two copies of the journal, safe temporary writes, and older game versions open
  newer saves read-only rather than damaging them.

## Not finished yet

- The fight tension layer and the two catch swells are still placeholder music.
- Other anglers on Hollow Creek and Arrow Point (after their shorelines are reshaped), in boats, and
  as tournament rivals.
- A narrator welcome on the main menu ("Welcome to Great American Fishing") is an idea for later.

*(Done since 25 Sept: the black boat's stripe, lettering and passenger console; jaws for smallmouth,
crappie, catfish and redeye, and their skeletons fixed; the Copper Bass Boat as boat 6; Tasha, Cole and
Reese; 16 computer anglers on eight lakes, with sound; the right hand staying on the rod in a fight on
every character; the licensed soundtrack, with sunset, dawn, night, rain, journal and lodge music.)*

text:
C.I.E. Tours - Scottish & Irish Gold
Starting from $5,245 Per Person

https://t.co/UnU5cSjtS4

Luxuriate in this grand tour
Explore some of the most historic cities and towns of Scotland and Ireland. Be enchanted by the Isle of Skye, St Andrews, Connemara, and the Ring of Kerry.

Tour start
Glasgow

Tour end
Dublin

16 Days
15 Nights
25 Meals

Day 1: Glasgow City Tour & Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum

Your journey begins with a 2:00 PM departure from your hotel for a panoramic tour of Glasgow. Once a powerhouse of industry, the city is now celebrated for its magnificent Victorian architecture, vibrant arts scene, excellent dining, and lively nightlife. Visit the renowned Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, home to one of Europe's finest collections, featuring works by masters such as Rembrandt, Titian, and Salvador Dalí. This evening, enjoy a welcome drink with your fellow travelers before spending the rest of the night exploring Glasgow at your leisure.

Day 2: Loch Lomond Cruise & Inveraray Castle

Cruise across the tranquil waters of Loch Lomond while admiring the surrounding Highland peaks. Stroll through the charming town of Inveraray before touring the magnificent Inveraray Castle, famously featured in Downton Abbey. Continue through the dramatic landscapes of Glencoe, one of Scotland's most breathtaking regions, before arriving at your hotel in Ballachulish on the shores of Loch Leven. (B, D)

Day 3: Isle of Skye & Loch Ness

Journey through Scotland's spectacular Highlands and cross onto the enchanting Isle of Skye. Enjoy lunch at Sligachan while taking in stunning views of the Cuillin Hills, then visit the historic Old Bridge, associated with legends of magical waters. Stop for photographs at the iconic Eilean Donan Castle before traveling along the scenic shores of Loch Ness to your hotel. (B, L, D)

Day 4: Culloden Battlefield & Sheepdog Demonstration

Explore the Culloden Battlefield Visitor Centre and learn about the pivotal Jacobite battle that shaped Scottish history. Take time to walk the historic moorland before continuing through the Highland landscape to a local farm, where expertly trained sheepdogs demonstrate their remarkable herding skills. This evening, relax in a charming manor-style hotel near Pitlochry. (B, D)

Day 5: Blair Castle & Whisky Tasting

Visit elegant Blair Castle, ancestral home of the Dukes and Earls of Atholl. Tour Blair Athol Distillery for an insider's look at Scotland's whisky-making tradition and sample its renowned single malt. Spend the afternoon at leisure, exploring Pitlochry's gardens, museums, and quaint town center. (B, D)

Day 6: Glamis Castle, St Andrews & Scottish Evening

Tour historic Glamis Castle, the legendary inspiration for Shakespeare's Macbeth. Continue to St Andrews, known worldwide as the "Home of Golf." Later, enjoy a traditional Scottish evening featuring regional cuisine, music, and entertainment. Departures between August 2 and August 23 enjoy an independent evening for dining. (B, D*)

Day 7: Edinburgh Castle & City Sightseeing

Discover Edinburgh on a panoramic city tour, from the medieval Royal Mile to the elegant Georgian streets of New Town. Visit the iconic Edinburgh Castle, perched high above the city with spectacular views. The remainder of the day is free for shopping, sightseeing, and dining. For departures between August 2 and August 23, enjoy the world-famous Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo on the Castle Esplanade. (B)

Day 8: Ferry to Belfast, Titanic Belfast & Dublin

Bid farewell to your Scottish guide and cruise across the Irish Sea to Belfast. Visit Titanic Belfast, an award-winning interactive attraction that tells the story of the famous ocean liner built nearby in 1912. Continue to Dun Laoghaire, a picturesque seaside suburb of Dublin, where you'll meet your Irish driver-guide and enjoy a free evening in this charming harbor town. (B)

Day 9: Sean's Bar & Galway Walking Tour

Travel to Athlone and enjoy a welcome drink at Sean's Bar, recognized as Europe's oldest pub. Continue to Galway, where a local guide introduces you to this vibrant coastal city known for its medieval streets, colorful atmosphere, and rich cultural heritage. Enjoy free time to explore before joining your group for dinner. (B, D)

Day 10: Connemara, Killary Harbour Cruise & Kylemore Abbey

Explore the rugged beauty of Connemara, one of Ireland's most scenic regions. Cruise aboard a catamaran on Killary Harbour, Ireland's only fjord (seasonal operation). Continue to Kylemore Abbey, beautifully situated beside a lake, and visit its elegant rooms, Gothic church, and Victorian walled gardens. Return to Galway for an evening at leisure. (B)

Day 11: Sheepdogs, Cliffs of Moher & Killarney

Travel through the dramatic landscapes of the Burren and visit a traditional sheep farm to watch skilled sheepdogs in action. Continue to the spectacular Cliffs of Moher, towering 700 feet above the Atlantic Ocean. Cross the Shannon Estuary by ferry before arriving in Killarney, where you'll enjoy dinner and traditional Irish entertainment at Kate Kearney's Cottage. (B, D)

Day 12: Jaunting Car Ride, Ring of Kerry & Kenmare

Experience a traditional horse-drawn jaunting car ride through Killarney National Park to scenic Ross Castle. Discover the highlights of the famed Ring of Kerry, one of Ireland's most scenic routes, with a stop in the colorful village of Kenmare. Visit the beautiful Gap of Dunloe before returning to Killarney for a free evening. (B)

Day 13: Blarney Castle, Irish Music & Waterford

Travel through scenic countryside to Blarney Castle, where you may climb to kiss the legendary Blarney Stone or simply enjoy the peaceful gardens. Continue along Ireland's southern coast to Dungarvan for an exclusive traditional music session at the Marine Bar. Arrive in Waterford, Ireland's oldest city, for a guided walking tour through its historic streets. (B, D)

Day 14: House of Waterford Crystal & Kilkenny Castle

Witness master craftsmen at work during a guided visit to the House of Waterford Crystal. Continue to medieval Kilkenny, where you'll have free time to explore before touring the beautifully restored Kilkenny Castle, renowned for its impressive collections, tapestries, and elegant interiors. Later, travel to Dublin and enjoy a farewell dinner with wine at One Ballsbridge. (B, D)

Day 15: Independent Dublin Exploration

Enjoy a flexible day discovering Dublin at your own pace with a Hop-On, Hop-Off sightseeing pass. Admission is included to one of Dublin's premier attractions, including the Guinness Storehouse, Teeling Distillery, EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum, Jameson Distillery Bow St. Experience, or the GPO Museum. (B)

Day 16: Farewell Dublin

Your unforgettable Scotland and Ireland adventure concludes after breakfast. (B)
