𝘽𝙚𝙮𝙤𝙣𝙙 𝙎𝙪𝙢𝙢𝙞𝙩: 𝙃𝙤𝙬 𝙐𝙎-𝘾𝙝𝙞𝙣𝙖 𝙩𝙞𝙚𝙨 𝙘𝙤𝙪𝙡𝙙 𝙨𝙩𝙞𝙡𝙡 𝙪𝙣𝙧𝙖𝙫𝙚𝙡

By Chow Chung-yan

𝗕𝗶𝗳𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗼𝗳 𝗠𝗼𝗼𝗱𝘀: 𝗨𝗽𝗯𝗲𝗮𝘁 𝘃𝘀 𝗗𝗼𝘄𝗻𝗯𝗲𝗮𝘁

Following the Trump-Xi summit in September, the mood on the Chinese MSM and social media was decidedly jollier and more upbeat that their counterparts in the U.S.

• Democrats criticised Trump’s cosying up to "communist" China as another example of his misguided foreign policy, a betrayal of American allies and even a sell-out of national interests.

• The MSM, locked in a feud with Trump over his ban on media access to the White House, either downplayed the visit or focused on its lack of tangible progress. Even the president’s allies admitted in private that the timing "was not right" to expect a major breakthrough.

• Even among Trump’s supporters and the business community, there is little agreement on what deals to seek with Beijing. 

With the midterm elections just weeks away, the polarisation of American politics can only deepen.

𝗔𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗼𝗿 𝗕𝗮𝗿 𝗖𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗖𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗮? 

Throughout the pre-sumnit negotiations, Americans certainly wanted China to lift its rare earth export controls, but there was no consensus on what to offer in return.
Two camps emerged:

• One camp argued that the restrictions will only push Beijing to accelerate its own chip development, and that it is in American interests to allow a controlled flow of advanced chips to China to maintain its "chip dependency".

• The other believes that China will pursue an alternative chip industry regardless, and that selling advanced chips would merely buy Beijing time. This camp holds that the US should double down on the restrictions, particularly as nobody can be sure whether China, or any other country, can really build an alternative system independent of American-controlled components.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and AMD CEO Lisa Su sat at the head table at the state dinner Trump hosted for Xi, but chip controls were never on the negotiating table. That suggests the hawks on this issue are in the driver’s seat.

𝗥𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗼𝗿 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗔𝗜? 

There is similarly no consensus among Americans on regulating AI. Some see regulation as a power grab by a handful of tech giants. Advocates of the open-source approach want to know how standards would be set, who would be responsible for verification, and how, even if a common set of standards could be agreed. 

The Chinese proposal to include chip controls in the bilateral AI dialogue only complicates matters. 

𝗔𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗼𝗿 𝗕𝗮𝗿 𝗖𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗼 𝗨𝗦?

The same is true of allowing more Chinese investment, or Chinese-owned EV and battery factories, in the U.S.. Some Chinese company executives travelled to Washington in the hope of a last-minute agreement that might open the door to US investment, but it proved futile.

Just a few days after Xi’s visit, Ford CEO Jim Farley warned that the US must carefully consider whether to admit Chinese carmakers to the American market, lest it become another Europe. Farley wants to work with the Chinese only in areas where America can acquire technologies it lacks, which is hardly something Beijing will be excited about.

𝗔𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗼𝗿 𝗕𝗮𝗿 𝗔𝗿𝗺𝘀 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗧𝗮𝗶𝘄𝗮𝗻? 

Beyond business, matters are even more complicated. It is widely known that Taiwan is Beijing’s absolute red line. Trump showed remarkable restraint on this sensitive issue throughout Xi’s visit, but even for him, the Chinese request that he openly oppose Taiwan independence was a bridge too far.

There is considerable pushback on the issue, even among Trump’s supporters. The president has delayed the latest round of arms sales to Taiwan, partly helped by supply shortages for more urgent needs elsewhere, but how long the administration can keep the lid on is an open question.

1/ Hello, Mike. Unlike just about every other response to the speech, this one is at least substantive. so I’ll return the favor. 

On the main, I don’t consider this a rebuttal to the speech so much as accepting the invitation to make the strict political case for ongoing support that I am saying is what is called for. 

Here are some point by point thoughts:

>You came to Jerusalem while the United States and Israel were engaged in a war against Iran… Yet you barely acknowledge the war, let alone consider what it reveals about the value of the alliance.

The purpose of the speech was not to make an analysis of the value of the alliance. In fact, I went out of my way to avoid doing so. This is perhaps our central disagreement. What the speech was (an attempt to describe drop in support and explain the macro trends for why) versus what you thought it ought to have been (a speech that also addresses all of those whys and rebuts them).

>”There is also a question of elementary respect. You came to a country at war to explain why Americans are growing weary of its demands on their attention and resources. You found time to discuss the immigration preferences of liberal American Jews and the political sins of the ADL, but not the soldiers fighting, the lives being lost, or the sacrifices being made in a common struggle. Whatever your intentions, that is a failure to recognize the gravity of the occasion.

I strenuously object to this point. I was invited here to give exactly this speech, on this topic, and was asked to deliver it bluntly. The audience, fwiw, by and large responded positively given their understanding of the context. 

>”And it is inseparable from the larger failure of your analysis. You tell us that Israel receives $3.8 billion annually in American assistance. But what does the United States receive in return? What is the value of Israeli intelligence, military power, technological innovation, and cooperation against common adversaries? What role does Israel play in America's competition with Iran, China, and Russia? What would it cost the United States to replace the capabilities and regional influence that the alliance provides?”

These are exactly the questions the speech is encouraging partisans to answer directly. Again, it is simply not the purview of the speech to offer these answers. 

>”These questions are the beginning of the prudential calculation you call for but never undertake.”

Correct. That is for others to do. 

>”what would happen if Washington weakened the relationship to the point that Israel concluded it could no longer rely on the United States?”

“…No sane Israeli wants that outcome…”

“…American support does not give Washington control over Israeli decisions…”

“..,And Israel would not be operating in a vacuum. China and Russia…”

“..,You call for realism while leaving the most consequential strategic questions unexamined.”

All of these paragraphs are answers to the question my speech is meant to tee up for others. More direct articulation of these points is exactly what’s needed. 

>”You never mention that Donald Trump, the dominant figure in the nationalist movement you describe, has taken American military cooperation with Israel to unprecedented levels.

“…How does his record fit your account of national conservatism? Why does the behavior of the nationalist president receive less attention than the attitudes of young nationalists? Is Trump an anomaly? Does he misunderstand the movement he leads? Or might his support for Israel reflect a nationalist assessment of American interests fundamentally different from the one you describe?

Trump is a unique transitionary figure. Time will tell wether his attitudes carry over into future iterations of the nationalist movement he currently leads, but I suspect successive generations on the right will not adopt his stance on this issue 1:1, and certainly wouldn’t depend on it.

text:
Wire · EU China trade · 9 Oct 2026

Maros Sefcovic has until Friday night to stop a trade war with China. The EU trade commissioner is in Beijing with Commerce Minister Wang Wentao, and the FT says Brussels already told ambassadors to prepare for failure.

The EU runs a goods deficit of more than €1bn a day with China. Plug-in hybrid imports are up 86% in the year to September while prices fell 20%. Brussels wants hybrids held to about 15% of the EU market, against more than a third today.

Beijing has rejected that cap and calls voluntary export limits a breach of WTO rules.

The EU has a model in mind.

In the 1980s Europe capped Japanese car exports and Nissan, Toyota and Honda built plants here. Now BYD starts in Szeged this year, Chery plans Barcelona and CATL is ramping up in Debrecen. An export cap plus local production would give the Commission a face-saving exit, Handelsblatt reports.

Europe is also weak where it counts, and it knows it. Diplomats note that even Washington had to back down once China limited rare earth exports. The Europeans know the same lever hits them.

Mercedes shows what the pressure looks like inside a company. Its China deliveries fell 29% in nine months, and about half of 2023 volume is left. Its new electric CLA sells under 100 a month there.

Sefcovic briefs ambassadors again on Sunday. EU leaders meet 15 and 16 October and choose between more talks and more tariffs. I would watch whether China offers anything beyond more investment and more imports.

Deep-Dive Analysis: MINISO Group Holding Limited ($MNSO  / https://t.co/UuYhKTBvWG)

-Dividend Yield of ~7%
-Buy Back Programm started for 10% of shares outstanding

0. Short Summary
MINISO is a global value retailer and IP pop-culture power station operating 8,600+ stores. 

Trading at an attractive valuation of ~4.5x EV/EBITDA, the company combines high-margin IP merchandise (Disney, Sanrio, proprietary IPs), rapid global store expansion (+37% North America revenue growth), strong cash generation, and an active HK$2.0B ($256M USD) share buyback program.   

1. Company Introduction
a. Company: 
Founded in 2013 in Guangzhou, MINISO Group Holding Limited is a leading B2C value and lifestyle retailer operating two core brands: "MINISO" and "TOP TOY".   
b. Shareholders & Capital Structure:
Founders & Insiders: 
Founder Mr. Ye Guofu and spouse Ms. Yang Yunyun hold 63.90%.   
Institutional Investors: 
~25% (Major holders include BNY Mellon at 9.4%, UBS Group at 7.8%, and HSBC at 6.0%).   
Retail / Free Float: ~11%.
Short Interest / Short Quote: Derivative hedging related to Equity Linked Securities accounts for ~15-18% reported short exposure (primarily market-neutral convertible arbitrage hedging rather than directional shorting).   

c. From Past to Future: 
Transitioned from a fast-fashion value retail store in China to a global IP-driven lifestyle platform with 8,674 stores worldwide as of June 2026 (4,665 MINISO China, 3,644 MINISO Overseas, 365 TOP TOY). 

The future strategy focuses on flagship formats (MINISO LAND, SUPER MINISO) and expanding global footprint in North America and Europe.   

d. Technology & Supply Chain: 
Tech-enabled agile supply chain launching 1,400+ new SKUs monthly. Advanced membership analytics driving a 132 million member ecosystem in mainland China (+31% YoY).   

2. Product Presentation & Current Developments
Core Pillars: 
Lifestyle products, beauty, and pop/blind-box toys.   

IP Strategy: Deep co-branding with Disney, Sanrio, Marvel, plus high-margin proprietary IPs like YOYO, Nommi, and Chou Chou.   

Store Format Evolution: 
Strategic rollout of large-format experience stores ("MINISO LAND", "SUPER MINISO", "MINISO SPACE"), boosting transaction value and customer dwell time.

Yonghui Superstores Integration: 
Holds a 29.4% strategic equity stake in Yonghui Superstores ($906M USD investment), which successfully turned profitable in H1 2026, contributing $8.7M USD (RMB 60.3M) in equity earnings.   

3. Valuation Snapshot
(Note: Exchange rate: 1 USD = 6.9194 RMB. Net Debt strictly excludes lease liabilities).   
Market Capitalization: ~$2.76 Billion USD (~1.20 Billion ordinary shares / 300 Million ADSs at ~$9.20/ADS).   

Total Cash & Liquid Investments: 
$1.068 Billion USD (RMB 7.39 Billion, including cash, term deposits, and liquid wealth management products).   
Total Financial Debt: $1.249 Billion USD (RMB 8.64 Billion, consisting of bank borrowings and cash-settled Equity Linked Securities; lease liabilities of $661.6M USD are excluded).   
Net Debt (Excluding Leases): $180.17 Million USD (RMB 1.25 Billion).   
Enterprise Value (EV): ~$2.9 Billion USD. 
  
Annualized Adjusted EBITDA: ~$680M - $700M USD (H1 2026 Adj. EBITDA reached $325.9M USD / RMB 2.26 Billion).

EV / Adjusted EBITDA Multiple: ~4.5x.   

4. Earnings Snapshot (H1 2026)
Revenue: $1.662 Billion USD (RMB 11.50 Billion), +22.4% YoY.   
Gross Profit: $736.2 Million USD (RMB 5.09 Billion); 
Gross Margin solid at 44.3%.   
Adjusted Operating Profit (ex FX): $235.4 Million USD (RMB 1.63 Billion), 
Adj. Operating Margin ex FX at 14.2%.   
Adjusted Net Profit (ex FX): $176.5 Million USD (RMB 1.22 Billion).   
Operating Cash Flow: $213.2 Million USD (RMB 1.48 Billion), representing a strong net profit conversion ratio of 1.37x.   

5. Peer Group Comparison
Pop Mart (Pop Toys): 
Trades at ~25x-30x EV/EBITDA due to high proprietary IP exposure. 

MINISO trades at a fraction of this (~6.0x EV/EBITDA) despite rapidly scaling its own TOP TOY brand (+32.7% YoY revenue growth).   

Five Below (US Value Retail): Trades at ~12x-15x EV/EBITDA with lower gross margins (~36% vs. MINISO's 44.3%) and slower international expansion.

Dollar General / Dollar Tree: Trade at ~10x-12x EV/EBITDA with low single-digit growth, whereas MINISO delivers 20%+ revenue CAGR expectations.   

6. Forecast 2030 (EBITDA & Valuation)
2030 Target Operational Metrics: 
Management targets long-term revenue CAGR of >=21%. 
Assuming 15,000+ stores globally by 2030 and higher IP revenue mix:   

Estimated 2030 Revenue: ~$5.8 Billion USD.

Estimated 2030 Adjusted EBITDA: ~$1.25 Billion USD (at ~21.5% EBITDA margin).

Valuation Target (EV/EBITDA): Re-rating to a conservative mid-cycle multiple of 10.0x-12.0x EV/EBITDA implies a target Enterprise Value of $12.5B - $15.0B USD, offering a potential 3.0x to 3.6x upside from the current EV of ~$4.14B USD.

7. Acquisition Potential
Hostile Takeover: 
Unlikely, as founders hold 63.90% voting/share ownership control.   

Private Equity Buyout / Go-Private Potential: 
High. 
Given the depressed 6.0x EV/EBITDA valuation, robust free cash flow generation ($108.5M USD FCF in H1 2026), and strong net cash position, MINISO presents an attractive target for a PE-led management buyout alongside founders.   

8. Catalysts / Milestones (Next 6–12 Months)
Share Repurchases: Execution of the HK$2.0 Billion ($256M USD) share buyback program authorized through June 2027.   

Store Acceleration in US & Europe: 
Rapid expansion of high-margin MINISO LAND flagships across primary US shopping centers.

Yonghui Remodeling Impact: Further operational turnaround and profitability gains at Yonghui Superstores boosting equity pick-up.   

Margin Expansion: 
Rising contribution of proprietary IPs (Nommi, YOYO) driving gross margin improvement.   

9. Opportunities & Risks
Opportunities: 
Unlocking global value IP retail market; aggressive expansion in North America (+37% YoY revenue); high operating cash flow conversion; dividend payout (~50% adjusted net profit policy).   

Risks: 
Geopolitical/trade tensions affecting global supply chain logistics; FX volatility; consumer sentiment fluctuations in China domestic offline retail.

10. Conclusion
MINISO is an unfairly discounted global retail winner trading at a deep value multiple of ~6.0x EV/EBITDA.

With a pristine balance sheet, surging international growth (+37% in North America), high insider alignment (63.9%), and massive share buybacks, MNSO offers compelling risk/reward for long-term B2C investors.

text:
What is corporate globalism and what is the difference between communist and Islamist sharia law systems?

The modern comparison between 20th-century communist takeovers and today’s corporate-driven globalism reveals a striking paradox: while both systems erode national sovereignty and consolidate power into fewer hands, they do so through entirely opposite economic models.

Critics and political theorists trace similarities in how both movements alter society, but they also note critical differences in their ultimate goals.

The Similarities: Consolidation and Social Engineering

Those who argue that globalism is a modern form of authoritarianism point to several operational parallels with historical regimes:

• Erosion of the Nation-State:

 • Communism: Aimed to dissolve national borders in favor of a global workers' revolution ("Workers of the world, unite!").

 • Corporate Globalism: 
Seeks to diminish national borders and local regulations to create a seamless, borderless marketplace for goods, capital, and labor.

• The Rise of a Managed Bureaucracy:

 • Communism: Power was concentrated in the hands of un-elected party bureaucrats (the Nomenklatura) who planned the entire economy.

 • Corporate Globalism:

 Power shifts toward un-elected international bodies, central banks, and multinational boardrooms that set global standards, trade rules, and ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) metrics.

• Utilization of Academic and Youth Movements:

 • Communism: Captured cultural and educational institutions to indoctrinate the youth, teaching them to reject traditional structures (family, religion, nation) in favor of the state.

 • Corporate Globalism: 
High-tech corporations and global foundations heavily fund university programs, promoting a "global citizen" identity. 

This encourages younger generations to view national borders and sovereignty as outdated or harmful concepts.

• The Illusion of Choice:

 • Communism: Offered a single-party state where the illusion of participation hid centralized control.

 • Corporate Globalism: 
Offers thousands of brands that are actually owned by a tiny handful of massive asset management firms (like BlackRock or Vanguard), creating a consumer market controlled by very few entities.

The Crucial Differences: Ideology vs. Capital

Despite these structural similarities, the economic engines and ultimate goals of the two systems are fundamentally opposed:

Feature 20th-Century Communism Modern Corporate Globalism
Core Goal Abolish private property, eliminate profit, and place production under absolute state control. 

Maximize private profit, expand corporate ownership, and open new global consumer markets.

How Power is Taken Through violent revolution, military force, state terror, and the total destruction of the capitalist class.

 Through economic leverage, lobbying, trade agreements & merging corporate interests with state power.

View on Wealth Billionaires and business owners R executed, imprisoned, or stripped of their assets. 

Billionaires & massive corporations hold the highest level of political influence and leverage.

Ultimate Destination A state-run monopoly where individual economic enterprise is illegal. 

A hyper-capitalist monopoly where global mega corporations control resources and traditional governments serve corporate interests.

The Result: "Technocratic Corporatism"

Most political scientists argue that the end goal of today's global elite is not a Soviet-style communist state, but rather a Technocracy or Corporatism (often referred to by critics as Stakeholder Capitalism).

In this system, private property isn't abolished by the state; instead, small private businesses are crushed by regulations and inflation, leaving only mega corporations standing.

The average citizen retains their nominal freedom but becomes entirely dependent on a centralized corporate-government apparatus 4 their housing, digital currency, employment, and information.

text:
Claude converts audio to full video stories

It’s that time again when we dive into the latest tech trends and see what’s shaking up our digital lives. Today, we’re talking about something truly groundbreaking—AI-generated videos from audio inputs. Yes, you heard right; Claude is leading the charge in transforming sound waves into visual stories.

So, how did this happen? Why now? And why should you care?
The Birth of AI-Generated Videos

Claude’s latest iteration has taken a significant leap by converting MP3 files into coherent video sequences. This isn’t just about creating GIFs from podcasts; it’s about generating full-fledged videos that tell a story based on the audio input. Imagine giving Claude an audiobook and getting back a visual novel in return.
How Does It Work?

Claude uses advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to analyze the audio content. The AI then generates visuals that align with the narrative or tone of the audio, creating a cohesive story rather than random images slapped together. This level of sophistication means that Claude can handle complex narratives and produce high-quality video output in real-time.

For example, if you upload an audiobook about a detective solving mysteries, Claude will generate scenes depicting crime scenes, suspects, and clues based on the narrative provided by the audio file. The AI’s ability to understand context and tone ensures that the visuals are not only visually appealing but also narratively sound.
What Changed?

The key development here is the ability to generate coherent visual stories from raw audio data. Previously, AI systems struggled with understanding context and narrative flow, but Claude has made significant strides in this area. The technology now allows for a more nuanced interpretation of spoken content, resulting in videos that are not only visually appealing but also narratively sound.
Concrete Use Cases

For businesses, this could mean streamlining workflows by generating video ads from voice scripts or creating visual interpretations of podcasts. As a consumer, you might soon be watching movies based on audiobooks or seeing visual stories that complement your favorite podcasts. Imagine being able to watch a movie adaptation of your favorite book without waiting for it to hit theaters.

For instance, imagine a podcast about space exploration. Claude could generate stunning visuals of planets, spacecraft, and astronauts in action, enhancing the listener’s experience by providing a full sensory immersion into the narrative.
What Is Stored?

Claude stores the audio input and generates corresponding video output in real-time. The system does not retain any personal data unless explicitly provided by the user during the generation process. This means that while the AI processes the audio, it doesn’t keep a record of your voice or other identifying information beyond what’s necessary for generating the video.
What Is Excluded?

While Claude can generate videos from MP3 files and spoken content, it does not handle text inputs directly to produce visual output. Additionally, the system is designed to work with publicly available audio sources; copyrighted material requires proper licensing before use.

For example, if you want to create a video based on an audiobook that has copyright restrictions, you would need to obtain permission from the rights holder before using Claude’s service.
User Controls

Users have control over the type of video generated by specifying parameters such as genre, mood, or specific elements they want included in the final product. For instance, you can ask Claude to generate a horror-themed video from an audiobook or a documentary-style video for a podcast episode.

This level of customization allows users to tailor the output to their preferences and needs, making it a versatile tool for both personal and professional use cases.
Availability

Claude’s video generation capabilities are currently available through its API and web interface. Users can upload audio files or provide voice inputs directly within the platform. The service is designed to be accessible to both individual users and businesses looking to integrate AI-generated content into their workflows.

For example, a marketing team could use Claude to quickly generate promotional videos from existing voice scripts, saving time and resources compared to traditional video production methods.
What This Does Not Prove

It's important to note that while Claude’s video generation capabilities are impressive, they do not prove that AI can replace human creativity entirely. The technology relies heavily on the quality of input data and the context provided by the user. Additionally, ethical considerations such as copyright infringement and privacy protection remain critical issues that need addressing.

For instance, even though Claude can generate visually stunning videos from audio inputs, it still requires a well-structured script or narrative to produce coherent content. The AI’s ability to understand and interpret complex human emotions and nuances is not yet on par with human creativity.
Practical Takeaway

For content creators, this technology offers a powerful tool to enhance storytelling and engage audiences in new ways. As AI continues to evolve, expect more advanced features and capabilities that will further blur the lines between human creativity and machine-generated content. The future is here, and it’s visual.

Got thoughts? Drop them in the comments below and let’s chat about this wild new frontier in AI-generated content. What do you think about Claude’s video generation capabilities? How might this technology impact your daily life or business?

So, there you have it—AI-generated videos are no longer a distant dream but an exciting reality shaping our digital future. Let the conversation begin!

text:
Some people are so desperate to manufacture a scandal that even a temporary petrol discount becomes “fuel subsidy reinstatement.” 😂

Let me explain this in the simplest language possible.

Imagine a market woman who buys a bag of rice for ₦70,000 and normally sells it for ₦80,000, making ₦10,000 profit. For the next 30 days, she decides to sell it for ₦70,000, giving up her entire ₦10,000 profit to make rice more affordable for her customers.

Has she started subsidising rice? NO! She has simply sacrificed her profit margin to offer temporary relief to her customers.

That is the distinction people are deliberately ignoring. NNPC's 30 day petrol discount initiative is about temporarily foregoing its retail profit margin, not automatically restoring the old fuel subsidy regime.

If a business temporarily gives up its profit to reduce the burden on customers, that does not automatically mean the government has reinstated a subsidy.

Please, let us stop confusing a temporary discount with a subsidy. You can criticise the policy, question its impact or demand more details, but twisting the facts to manufacture a scandal does not make you intelligent.

You cannot turn a discount into a subsidy by shouting louder. Facts are stubborn, no matter how hard propaganda tries to bend them. 🇳🇬🔥

His ministers and senators are being chased like thieves whenever they gather among the people. The hardship has become so unbearable that political loyalty and party slogans are struggling to compete with empty stomachs.

Maybe they have finally told Daddy that a mini bag of rice is no longer enough.

So, what does Daddy do? He adds a litre of petrol to the package! 👏

Remember, the subsidy was gone forever. Gone! Buried! Never to return!

But here we are, with a 30-day petrol discount at NNPC stations. Not a subsidy, o! A discount!

But wait, what happened to the CNG cars that were supposed to arrive on October 1 to make transportation cheaper? Another poorly crafted promise from short-sighted leaders. I guess Daddy doesn’t even know that the contractor may have sold him another dream.

Daddy, what exactly does Daddy know? Macron’s lullaby can no longer let our Daddy hear the sounds.

After all, what is the point of worrying about the cries when there are international friendships to nurture abroad?

And talking about friendship, imagine befriending a president rejected by several of his own former colonies, and now he is coming to Nigeria for a state visit. 🥲

What exactly are you hoping to share with him? His political troubles? His unpopularity?

Will he be coming to Nigeria to beg or perhaps to borrow money to pay teachers’ salaries in France? And according to the announced agenda, they will be discussing trade and investment, mining, and energy.

This is how you know when a country’s leadership is heading for the rocks: the people are asking for solutions, but their president is busy collecting international, parasitic friendships.

Friendship with a country that offers little tangible value in return, yet somehow commands the prestige of a relationship simply because it is foreign.

This is possible because some of the people leading Nigeria appear so foreign-struck that anything from abroad excites them.

So, while a mini bag of rice now needs a litre of petrol to make its way into the household budget, Tinubu is still trying to figure out what else to add to the package.

And now, they tell us it is a discount, not a subsidy.

Please, somebody help us define the word subsidy and explain how it differs in the context of this arrangement.

🤣 The moment Nigeria became friends with Macron, it showed that only the crumbs were left of our leadership, with no other world leader wanting to come close.

PLANT HEMP, DO NO HARM (continued)

Meanwhile, precaution is ignored where it matters most. In 2015 the World Health Organization's cancer agency classified glyphosate as probably carcinogenic to humans. It is found in the urine of most people tested, and it is still sprayed on our food. Synthetic biology is on your agenda in Yerevan, yet engineered organisms released into soil, water or air can never be called back. And mRNA products are spreading into people, animals and farms faster than independent, long-term safety evidence can be gathered.

No harm to the living earth and no harm to the living body are one principle, and you have written it into law again and again. Article 7 of your International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights forbids medical or scientific experimentation on any person without free consent. Article 4 of the same Covenant says that right can never be suspended, not even in an emergency. UNESCO's Declaration on the Human Genome requires prior, free and informed consent for anything that touches a person's genes. The Nuremberg Code opens with the words "The voluntary consent of the human subject is absolutely essential."

Canada's Charter of Rights and Freedoms, the courts of the United States since 1914, and English law from Magna Carta to today all say the same: a person decides what is done to their own body. As John Stuart Mill wrote, "Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign."

In my view, the emergency orders of the COVID-19 years broke these laws by making work, travel, school and family life depend on an injection with no long-term record. An emergency does not suspend Article 7. I see the same pattern returning now with mRNA and with our food. No government, agency or emergency order may tell a man or woman what must enter their body.

So I ask you, plainly:

1. Name hemp grown in permaculture as a priority pathway in the 2030 Agenda and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

2. Urge every Member State to remove the barriers that stop people from growing hemp on their own land.

3. Remove psilocybin mushrooms from Schedule I, so whole plants and fungi are not illegal while their isolated parts are patented.

4. Apply the precautionary principle to glyphosate, to every release of engineered organisms, and to mRNA products, and halt them until independent, long-term safety evidence is public.

5. End medical mandates. No person may be coerced, or made to lose work, travel or schooling, for refusing any medical product, under any emergency.

6. Fund research into whole-plant hemp medicine and hemp materials with the urgency you give to patented technologies.

I offer a way forward without war and without fighting. Sun Tzu taught that "the supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting." Better still is to have no enemy at all. End the divide and conquer. Do not let money, greed and control stand in the way. Gandhi reminded us that "the earth provides enough to satisfy every man's needs, but not every man's greed."

The prophet Micah promised a day when "they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid." Plant hemp, and that day comes closer.

Before you vote in Yerevan, ask yourselves one question: what color is your soul?

No harm, no trespass.

In service to the living earth and all who live upon her,

text:
He wasn't martyred.
Historically speaking, Jesus was probably arrested and executed as a criminal for his temper tantrum in the Jewish Temple. 
The Synoptics place the temper tantrum in the final week of Jesus's life near the end of ministry
John's Gospel is the only Gospel that places it near the beginning of his ministry.

In regard to Christian mythology/theology (i.e. the Gospel narrative), the Jews wanted him killed for blasphemy as he claimed to be the "Son of Man," who was given authority, glory, sovereign power, and an everlasting kingdom.
The Sanhedrin couldn't execute him (only the Roman governor possessed the "jus gladii"), so the High Priest handed him off to Pontius Pilate to be executed.
As per the narrative in Matthew, Pontius Pilate offered the crowd a choice based on the Jewish custom of pardoning a prisoner during Passover: should they release Jesus or should they release a rebel/insurrectionist named Barabbas? 
This figure "Barabbas" was a literary creation rather than a real prisoner.
The meaning of the name is literally "Son of the Father."
The Jews choose to free Barabbas.
Pilate then interrogates Jesus, sees no fault or crime in him, and washes his hands to declare his innocence of Jesus's blood.
The Romans subsequently give him a crown of thorns, whip him and crucify him.
Note, however, how the narrative never states that the Romans or the Jews had the capacity to kill him.
In contrast, Jesus says he could call on his "father" (God) and his father would send 12 legions of angels (i.e. 72,000 angels) to assist him in Gethsemane, yet he chose not to do so.
He also says "No one takes it [i.e. my life] from Me, but I lay it down Myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it up again. I received this command from My Father."
So even by the Christian account, he was not a martyr because he laid down his life himself.

text:
WOMAN, YOUR SENSUALITY IS A SHIELD FOR YOU.

Not a costume. Not a bargain. Not a door left ajar for whoever knocks loudest. It is the living membrane between your soul and the world—dense, luminous, and older than language. The ancients knew this: the veil was never meant only to hide, but to sanctify what it covered. Your body remembers the same law.

Sensuality, when it is yours, is not performance. It is boundary made flesh. The way heat rises from skin, the way breath lengthens, the way attention gathers and withdraws—these are not invitations by default. They are the outer rings of an inner temple. What you offer freely is gift. What you withhold is architecture. Both are holy.

Many have tried to rename this power as weakness, or as debt, or as something that must be spent to be real. That is a theft of language. A shield does not apologize for being hard where it must be hard and warm where it chooses to be warm. It does not explain its metal. It simply holds.

So let the current move through you without surrendering the gate. Let desire be a river that knows its banks. Let beauty be a lantern you carry, not a fire you are required to feed strangers with. The ones who can meet you will recognize the shield and bow to it. The ones who cannot will call it cold, or proud, or unfinished. Let them. Their names do not enter the inner court.

Woman, your sensuality is not the absence of protection. It is the protection—woven of nerve and myth, of silence and pulse, of the ancient right to remain sovereign inside your own skin.

Tanker freight rates soaring to record highs are putting US crude oil out of reach for Asian refiners, pushing them to seek alternatives from the Middle East and Latin America, according to Reuters sources. (RTRS)

The closed plants represented almost 20% of California’s refining capacity, but reopening would face substantial hurdles. (WSJ)

Australia plans to introduce legislation next week requiring LNG producers to reserve up to 20% of output for domestic buyers, Bloomberg sources said. No exporter is expected to receive a full exemption; Queensland projects face the biggest impact. (BBG)

MACRO:

Technical selling pressure amplifying the Treasury rout may be easing: mortgage-bond durations are approaching their extension limits, while Goldman says pressure from Treasury-futures switches has diminished. Morgan Stanley cautions that mortgage-related hedging may still have further to run. (WSJ)

Pimco CIO Dan Ivascyn told the FT that US 10-year yields could hit 6% as leveraged investors are forced to unwind losing bond positions. He warned that yields of 5.5% or above would bring meaningful weakness in equities and credit. (FT)

Franklin Templeton CEO Jenny Johnson favours short-dated tech debt over longer maturities, citing increasingly complex financing structures and technological uncertainty. “Two-year paper at nine, pretty dang good!” she told Bloomberg TV. (BBG)

Hurricane Isaias’s projected direct threat to US refining narrowed to just under 500kb/d, from approximately 2.5mb/d earlier in the week. Most Louisiana refining capacity is now expected to avoid a direct hit, with Alabama and Mississippi facilities still exposed. (S&P Global)

Democratic Reps. Sara Jacobs and Don Beyer are preparing AI legislation requiring minimum safety standards and clarifying liability. The proposed framework would give the government emergency power to shut down models that fail testing requirements. (Politico)

Japan’s real household spending fell 3.1% Y/Y in August versus a 3.6% decline expected, its ninth consecutive monthly contraction despite rising wages. Spending edged up just 0.1% M/M. (BBG)

Japan is considering a review of up to ¥7tn in unused government funds to help finance Takaichi’s agenda and limit additional borrowing. The amount that could actually be recovered remains unclear. (BBG)

Takaichi told parliament that stronger growth and competitiveness would help sustain confidence in the yen, arguing her fiscal agenda is consistent with currency support. She said authorities would monitor the yen’s impact on prices and act when necessary. (BBG)

Foreign investors sold a record ¥2.24tn of Japanese equity futures in the week ended October 2 while buying ¥956bn of cash equities. The divergence points to substantial hedging alongside continued stock purchases. (BBG)

China’s Star 50 index fell as much as 4.6%, taking its two-day decline beyond 9%, as concerns over the global AI trade hit expensive hardware stocks. ChiNext dropped as much as 3.4%. (BBG)

China’s Golden Week new-home sales rose 15% Y/Y across 25 cities after fresh stimulus, according to Proptech data, but remained 9% below 2024. The improvement suggests only a modest recovery despite mortgage subsidies. (BBG)

Foreign borrowers have issued ¥115.5bn of panda bonds this year, roughly double the full-year 2025 total, as cheap Chinese funding and easier overseas use of proceeds draw demand. (BBG)

The London Metal Exchange should allow its members to clear trades in offshore yuan because the Chinese currency is becoming important for Asian trade flows, Marc Bailey, CEO of broker Sucden Financial, told Reuters. (RTRS)

Iron ore fell toward its lowest since September 2024 as Chinese port stocks climbed to 152.7m tonnes. Fewer than 7% of Chinese steel mills are profitable, raising the risk of further output cuts, according to data cited by Bloomberg. (BBG)

Brussels is pushing back against Italian and Greek requests for more fiscal flexibility in their 2027 budgets. EU economy commissioner Dombrovskis warned that repeatedly relaxing the rules would undermine confidence in fiscal sustainability. (FT)

Europe’s funding squeeze is prompting analysts to call for cheaper ECB refinancing operations as bank reserves head toward €2tn, from a €4.5tn peak. Repo rates have reached their highest since March 2025, with heavy sovereign issuance adding pressure. (BBG)

European banks face additional scrutiny of their more than €4tn sovereign-bond holdings as yields rise, EBA chair François-Louis Michaud told Bloomberg. He described exposure as “contained” so far, with stronger interest income helping offset valuation losses. (BBG)

UK PM Burnham adviser Jim O’Neill told the FT that Chancellor Healey should let fiscal headroom shrink by £10bn rather than raise taxes in this month’s Budget. He particularly opposed higher capital gains tax and questioned the benefit of another bank tax increase. (FT)

The UK’s ONS plans to introduce a seasonally adjusted monthly inflation measure early next year, giving traders a US-style gauge of underlying price momentum alongside existing CPI releases. (BBG)

Norway's annual core inflation rate remained at 3.0% year-on-year in September, Statistics Norway (SSB) data showed on Friday, supporting expectations that interest rates will stay elevated. (RTRS)

Labour held Starmer’s former Holborn and St Pancras seat, defeating Green leader Zack Polanski by 12,292 votes to 8,928. The result comes after Burnham’s government delayed decisions on two North Sea fossil fuel projects until after the vote. (FT)

Cold Lake First Nations filed the first legal challenge to Canada’s fast-tracking of the Pacific Link oil pipeline, alleging inadequate consultation. The proposed line would carry 1mln bpd to the west coast as part of Carney’s export-diversification push. (BBG)

The full impact of a workers' strike at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine in Chile is expected to be felt in November, when production could decrease by half, unions said on Thursday. (RTRS)

Brazil’s Datafolha runoff poll put Flávio Bolsonaro at 52% versus Lula at 48% of valid votes. The October 6–7 survey interviewed 2,520 people, with a ±2-point margin of error. (Datafolha via Eixo Político)

Polish central banker Ludwik Kotecki said that if inflation projections do not show it returning close to 2.5% by the end of 2027 or start of 2028, then a 25-basis-point rate hike would be necessary in November, PAP agency reported on Friday. (RTRS)

Uruguay raised rates 25bp to 6%, its first hike since April 2025, after inflation moved above its 4.5% target. Policymakers said the aim was to prevent temporary food and energy increases spreading into broader prices and expectations. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

The US is seizing seven internet domains allegedly used by China’s Integrity Technology Group to help hackers target US and foreign critical infrastructure. The Justice Department described it as its second public operation against the company’s hacking infrastructure. (RTRS)

A US arms package for Taiwan worth up to $14bn remains in limbo ahead of further Trump–Xi meetings, Bloomberg reported. Washington has continued diplomatic engagements and existing weapons deliveries, but announced no change in Taiwan policy. (BBG)

The Pentagon has struck more than a dozen preliminary agreements to accelerate munitions production, but Congress has yet to fund most of them, WSJ reports. Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg says the multiyear commitments are intended to encourage manufacturers to expand capacity. (WSJ)

Israel has expanded its control of Gaza to around 70%, according to Netanyahu, versus 53% under the ceasefire agreement, while fortifying more than 30 military bases. People familiar with negotiations expect no progress on the next phase of the peace plan before Israel’s October 27 election. (WSJ)

Poland activated military aviation and temporarily closed Lublin and Rzeszów airports during Russian air attacks on western Ukraine. Polish authorities issued alerts in the adjoining regions. (Polish air-navigation agency, Government Security Centre)

EQUITIES:

OpenAI expects annualised revenue to reach or exceed $70bn by year-end, versus roughly $50bn at end-September, driven mainly by enterprise growth, Bloomberg sources said. The figures were shared during discussions for a $30bn-plus raise at a $1.4tn pre-money valuation. (BBG)

Apple has reportedly told suppliers to cut production of components for its iPhone 18 and Pro Max as rising prices dampens consumer demand, Nikkei reports. "In October alone, we are seeing orders from Apple reducing by 15% to 20% for both the premium models; we don't know how things would develop from here". (Nikkei)

SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son is seeking up to $100bn from Gulf investors for a fund that would buy companies and improve their operations using AI, people familiar told the FT. Discussions include senior UAE figures; funding is not assured. (FT)

Shares of Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile US all fell signifcantly after hours after SpaceX announced a spectrum acquisition supporting a direct-to-consumer Starlink mobile network. SpaceX plans to combine satellite and terrestrial coverage, subject to final FCC approval. (FT)

Humana surged 17% in late trading after its largest Medicare Advantage contract, covering more than 2m members, regained a bonus-qualifying quality rating. The improvement boosts its 2028 revenue outlook; CVS and Alignment fell following their own ratings results. (BBG)

Nvidia-backed Firmus formally abandoned its Australian IPO and will seek alternative funding, including private capital and potentially a US listing. The offering had targeted up to $5.5bn at a $30bn valuation, versus a $10.5bn valuation less than three months earlier. (BBG)

Nvidia plans to invest in AI-chip rival d-Matrix, extending its push to bring competing chipmakers into its hardware ecosystem. (The Information)

Lumentum’s optical-component capacity is “completely sold out” through early 2029, CEO Michael Hurlston told Bloomberg. The Nvidia-backed supplier cannot meet roughly 70% of demand for some products through 2027 and plans at least $350m of investment in Japan. (BBG)

Meta banned ByteDance from advertising across its apps in seven countries, including the US, Canada and Japan, extending the block to third-party ads linking to TikTok. Meta said it need not carry ads for a competitor seeking to pull users away. (BBG)

American Express was fined $350m by US regulators over anti-money-laundering failures involving roughly $13bn of suspicious transactions. Amex said the action would not affect 2026 guidance; shares fell about 2%. (BBG)

The Pentagon is providing Palantir up to $244mn for its War Machine platform to improve manufacturing efficiency at defence contractors, according to documents and people cited by WSJ. The funding is additional to Palantir’s other Pentagon work. (WSJ)

Southwest is leaning toward Boeing’s 787 for a potential long-haul international expansion, Reuters reports. The airline could seek dozens of aircraft and launch services in roughly three years, but no final board decision has been made. (Reuters)

Walmart’s multibillion-dollar warehouse automation programme is encountering robot breakdowns and difficulties handling merchandise, WSJ reports. Supplier Symbotic has struggled to meet throughput targets as Walmart retrofits facilities while keeping them operational. (WSJ)

Memory shortages could persist at least through H1 2027, industry participants told CNA. Micron’s second Taichung advanced-packaging plant is scheduled to start mass production in mid-October, while its acquired Tongluo fab is expected to add capacity in H2 2027. (CNA)

SK Chairman Chey Tae-won said on Friday that chipmaker SK Hynix plans to build plants in southwestern South Korea as fast as possible, betting on robust demand growth, while declining to say when construction will begin. (RTRS)

SK chairman Chey Tae-won said chip demand is expected to continue growing rapidly, speaking during a visit to SK Hynix’s planned semiconductor hub in South Korea. (RTRS)

According to Korean media reports, Samsung Electronics has already secured long-term agreements (LTAs) covering 75–80% of its memory supply volume for next year, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM). (Hankyung via @jukan05)

Samsung’s 12-layer HBM4E has reportedly passed customer quality validation at Nvidia and major hyperscalers, according to DigiTimes. (DigiTimes)

Xiaomi jumped as much as 9.2% after reporting more than 70,000 orders for its SkyNomad SUV in its first month. Goldman called the disclosure supportive of the EV growth story, although below the most bullish expectations. (BBG)

UBS executives are resigned to losing the fight against proposed Swiss capital requirements, the FT reports. Its analysis examines relocation and merger options, but a senior employee expects UBS to stay and adapt; no Morgan Stanley transaction is currently being pursued. (FT)

Porsche said on Friday it delivered 16% fewer vehicles globally in the first nine months of 2026, as weak demand in China, the phase-out of the 718 model line and its focus on brand value over volume continued to weigh on sales. (RTRS)

BASF could make a higher offer for Evonik if there are talks with the specialty chemicals maker, sources close to BASF told Reuters on Friday. (RTRS)

Airtel Money priced its London IPO at £1.96, raising about £529m for selling shareholders and valuing the company at £5.3bn. Trading starts Friday in London’s largest IPO for five years, after the company twice lowered valuation expectations. (BBG)

Maersk ordered 26 ships in September, taking its order book to 131 as it defends its position against CMA CGM. CEO Vincent Clerc says persistent disruption has created a floor under freight rates and the group will compete more aggressively. (FT)

Glencore expects strong demand from investors seeking exposure to trend toward electrification when it lists in Australia next week, CEO Gary Nagle said on Friday, adding that a deeper local presence may yield business opportunities although it has no set buyout list. (RTRS)

Jio’s IPO roadshow met resistance over its roughly $114bn valuation target, with investors questioning its premium to Bharti Airtel and how free digital services will be monetised, Bloomberg sources said. Pricing could fall further before the planned late-October listing. (BBG)

text:
“God will give you grace for what you are carrying today.” ❤️

Well, I don’t often get on my soapbox, but today I need to share something from my heart.

I’m feeling kind of exhausted.

Fifteen months ago, my husband and I stepped away from jobs we loved, a community we cherished, and the precious grandchildren we adored being near. Why? Because we believed God was opening a door we had prayed about for years.

For over two years, we had been meeting, praying, and planning with a woman who had approached us about managing her beautiful 40-acre property near Jacksonville, Florida. Our dream was to establish our first Comfort Bags for Kids Rescue Ranch, a place of healing, safety, and restoration for young children (ages 3-12)  rescued from trafficking and exploitation.

Everything seemed to be falling into place.

Beautiful horses had been donated. Veterinary care, feed, and equine therapy resources had been offered. Mission teams were ready to help restore the ranch facilities. We had raised funds and were preparing to welcome children who desperately needed a safe place to heal.

After 27 years in full-time children’s ministry, I stepped away from my position. My husband left the special education school where he had faithfully served for 11 years.

We weren’t running away from anything. We were running toward what we believed God was calling us to do.

And then everything fell apart.

There is no way to share all the painful details here, but after relocating to Florida, we discovered that the woman we had trusted had seriously misrepresented things to us. In fact, people hundreds of miles away knew of her reputation before we ever mentioned her name.

We felt deceived. Humiliated. Heartbroken.

And yes, we felt foolish.

But perhaps the hardest part wasn’t what happened to us. It was grieving a dream that had seemed so close to becoming a reality, a dream that involved bringing healing to precious children.

Since then, we’ve spent 15 months trying to regain our footing, discern God’s direction, and figure out what comes next.

And quite frankly, it’s been exhausting.

Recently, my husband experienced a frightening illness that required hospitalization. Praise God, he is recovering beautifully! But we are now facing some significant decisions about our future, our ministry, and where God wants us to serve.

So today, I’m simply asking for prayer.

Not sympathy. Not answers. Just prayer.

We still believe in the calling God placed on our hearts. We still believe in the mission of Comfort Bags for Kids. And we still believe that God can bring beauty from ashes.

But I am also learning that being a person of faith doesn’t mean we never become weary.

Sometimes faith looks like getting up another morning and saying, “Lord, I don’t know what comes next, but I still trust You.”

And that’s where I am today.

I’m holding tightly to the words I began with:

“God will give you grace for what you are carrying today.”

Not necessarily grace for next month or next year. But grace for today.

Thank you to everyone who has prayed for us, encouraged us, and loved us through this unexpected season.

Our dream may have been interrupted, but our calling has not disappeared.

And I believe with all my heart that God is not finished writing our story.

One day at a time. One prayer at a time. One step of faith at a time.

text:
19:43 SWITZERLAND 🇨🇭 | 12:43 CME / CHICAGO 🇺🇸
NQ / NASDAQ — LATE-SESSION REGIME RADAR
8 OCT 2026
MAIN CONCLUSION: Thursday has confirmed that the principal threat to NQ is no longer simply the Fed. Oil, long-term Treasury yields and competition for capital are now interacting directly with technology valuations. Nasdaq remains only modestly below its recent record despite a powerful energy shock and 5.3%+ yields, but the session has exposed the growing cost of maintaining the AI investment cycle in an increasingly expensive capital environment.
KEY CONFIRMATION / RISK: The strongest positive development of the afternoon is that the $22 billion 30-year Treasury auction attracted solid demand, helping long yields retreat from their intraday extremes. That prevented the bond sell-off from becoming disorderly. The key question now is whether this is enough to stabilise the discount-rate environment while oil remains above $100 and technology breadth stays fragile.
TODAY WAS A MACRO STRESS TEST, NOT A NORMAL PULLBACK
The most important feature of Thursday is not simply that Nasdaq traded lower.
It is what the market had to absorb.
Brent surged more than 4% and traded above $104.
WTI moved above $92.
The US 10Y returned towards the 5.3% region.
The 30Y remained near multi-decade highs.
The dollar stayed firm.
Semiconductors weakened.
And the market simultaneously began debating whether the enormous debt required to fund AI infrastructure could itself become another source of upward pressure on the cost of capital.
Against that backdrop, NQ has not collapsed.
That is still evidence of considerable underlying demand.
OIL WAS THE FIRST SHOCK OF THE DAY
The energy move was the most immediate macro catalyst.
Brent surged towards the mid-$100s while WTI moved above $92 as geopolitical and supply risks intensified.
That matters because oil is now directly connected to the NQ regime through inflation expectations.
The transmission mechanism is straightforward:
OIL ↑ → INFLATION RISK ↑ → TERM PREMIUM ↑ → LONG YIELDS ↑ → TECHNOLOGY VALUATION PRESSURE.
Earlier in the week, falling oil helped ease financial conditions.
Today that entire relationship reversed.
The energy market once again became a headwind rather than a tailwind.
BUT OIL DID NOT HOLD THE EXTREME
An important development later in the session was that crude gave back part of the initial surge.
That matters.
A market dealing with Brent at $105+ and still accelerating is substantially more dangerous than one where the energy shock begins stabilising.
For NQ, the distinction is not cosmetic.
The market can price a high but stable oil environment.
It has much more difficulty pricing an uncontrolled energy acceleration.
That means the late-session moderation in crude reduced one of the most immediate tail risks.
It did not eliminate the inflation problem.
THE 10Y REMAINS AROUND THE CRITICAL 5.3% AREA
The US 10Y is still trading close to the region that has repeatedly acted as the market's macro stress threshold.
That remains one of the most important relationships on the screen.
NQ has proven it can tolerate a 10Y above 5%.
It has even demonstrated that 5.3% is survivable.
But the market struggles when yields begin accelerating beyond that area while other conditions also tighten.
Today's early move again tested that boundary.
The fact that yields later eased matters because it prevented the session from developing into a full rates shock.
THE 30Y AUCTION WAS THE MOST IMPORTANT POSITIVE EVENT
The Treasury sold approximately $22 billion of 30-year bonds this afternoon.
Demand was solid.
That matters because the long end has been at the centre of this week's global bond stress.
The auction showed that current yields are beginning to attract buyers even at the longest maturities.
This does not mean the Treasury problem is solved.
But it reduces the probability that the market immediately needs dramatically higher yields simply to absorb supply.
That is important for technology valuations.
THIS WEEK'S TREASURY AUCTIONS HAVE SENT A MESSAGE
The 3-year auction was absorbed well.
The 10-year auction was strong.
The 30-year auction was solid.
That sequence matters.
The market has spent the week worrying that Treasury supply would overwhelm demand and force yields continuously higher.
The auction results have not validated that extreme fear.
Investors are still willing to absorb US duration.
The problem is that even with healthy demand, yields remain historically elevated.
That tells us the market is not simply suffering from bad auctions.
The structural forces behind high yields remain powerful.
THE PROBLEM IS BROADER THAN TREASURY SUPPLY
The Fed remains restrictive.
Oil remains elevated.
Inflation remains persistent.
Term premium remains high.
Global sovereign yields are under pressure.
Fiscal concerns remain unresolved.
And now large technology and AI-related companies are increasingly entering debt markets to finance enormous infrastructure investment.
That means capital demand is coming from several directions simultaneously.
Governments need capital.
AI companies need capital.
Energy infrastructure needs capital.
Data centres need capital.
Power generation needs capital.
The result is a much more competitive market for duration.
That competition itself can keep yields higher.
AI FINANCING IS BECOMING PART OF THE MACRO STORY
This may be the most important structural development of the week.
For years, AI investment was viewed almost exclusively as an earnings accelerator.
More capex meant more chips.
More chips meant more data-centre capacity.
More capacity meant more revenue.
That remains true.
But the scale of AI infrastructure spending is now creating another effect.
The industry increasingly requires enormous amounts of borrowed capital.
That introduces a new relationship:
AI CAPEX ↑ → FUTURE EARNINGS ↑
but also
AI BORROWING ↑ → CAPITAL DEMAND ↑ → CREDIT SUPPLY PRESSURE ↑ → YIELD PRESSURE ↑.
This is the first time the AI boom itself may be contributing to the denominator used to value AI earnings.
That deserves serious attention.
THE NUMERATOR / DENOMINATOR FRAMEWORK IS CHANGING
The numerator remains exceptionally strong.
TSMC reported record sales.
Samsung delivered an extraordinary profit increase.
AI infrastructure demand remains powerful.
Cloud and data-centre investment continue expanding.
Those are genuine fundamental signals.
But the denominator is also becoming more demanding.
Treasury yields are high.
Oil is high.
Corporate borrowing is increasing.
The dollar remains firm.
And the cost of capital remains historically restrictive.
That means the market increasingly needs extraordinary earnings growth simply to justify maintaining present valuations.
That is a tougher equilibrium.
STRONG SEMICONDUCTOR FUNDAMENTALS DID NOT PROTECT THE STOCKS
One of today's most important market signals was the disconnect between fundamentals and price.
TSMC delivered very strong revenue.
Samsung reported a dramatic profit increase.
Yet semiconductor shares remained under pressure.
That tells us the market is no longer responding to strong chip fundamentals in isolation.
Investors are demanding answers to a second question:
How much capital must be spent to generate the next stage of AI growth?
That is different from asking whether AI demand is strong.
The demand is strong.
The debate is increasingly about the cost and financing of that demand.
THIS DOES NOT MEAN THE AI TRADE IS BROKEN
The distinction is important.
Nothing in today's session proves that AI demand is weakening structurally.
The opposite may be true.
What is changing is the price the market is willing to pay for those future earnings when the risk-free rate and corporate borrowing costs are so high.
That means today's weakness is better described as:
VALUATION COMPRESSION RISK
rather than
AI DEMAND COLLAPSE.
Those are completely different regimes.
FED MINUTES ARE STILL RELEVANT
Wednesday's FOMC minutes showed that most policymakers still expected additional tightening to be required.
That keeps December very much alive even though October appears much less likely.
The policy structure is therefore becoming clearer:
OCTOBER PAUSE POSSIBLE.
DECEMBER STILL LIVE.
LONG-END PRESSURE INDEPENDENTLY HIGH.
For NQ, this means monetary relief cannot simply be assumed.
The Fed may pause.
The bond market may still remain restrictive.
TODAY'S LABOUR MESSAGE DID NOT CHANGE THE REGIME
The labour data did not create the kind of decisive shift that Friday's payroll report produced.
That is important.
The market has already moved beyond a simple narrative where weaker employment automatically means lower yields and higher NQ.
Oil, inflation and term premium now matter enough to complicate that relationship.
This is exactly why we have been emphasizing reaction rather than headline data.
A softer labour signal can no longer guarantee a dovish market response if energy prices and long-term borrowing costs remain under pressure.
THE SESSION HAS SHOWN RESILIENCE — BUT NOT STRENGTH
There is an important difference.
NQ has not delivered a powerful bullish reversal.
But neither has it suffered the kind of liquidation one might expect from the day's macro backdrop.
That means the correct description is:
RESILIENCE, NOT EXPANSION.
Buyers remain present.
But they are no longer receiving help from the macro environment.
That reduces the quality of the bullish regime.
BREADTH REMAINS AN IMPORTANT WARNING
The market has become increasingly dependent on a relatively narrow group of large technology names.
That concentration has been a recurring theme.
When semiconductor breadth weakens at the same time that long yields remain elevated, the index becomes more fragile.
A narrow market can keep rising.
But it has less internal support when the leaders finally weaken.
That is why SOX remains one of the most important confirmation indicators for NQ.
THE EQUITY RISK PREMIUM IS NOW EXTREMELY TIGHT
There is another structural issue developing.
With Treasury yields above 5%, investors can earn historically attractive returns without accepting equity risk.
That changes the competitive relationship between bonds and stocks.
When the risk-free return rises while equity valuations remain elevated, the compensation investors receive for owning stocks becomes increasingly compressed.
This does not force equities lower immediately.
But it raises the hurdle for future returns.
Technology therefore needs stronger earnings growth to remain attractive relative to bonds.
Again, the earnings numerator must work harder.
THE 30-YEAR AUCTION PROVIDES SOME RELIEF
The auction therefore matters beyond today's basis-point move.
It tells us that investors are still willing to buy duration even under these conditions.
That reduces the immediate risk of a disorderly bond-market event.
For NQ, this is helpful.
A controlled high-yield environment is much easier to manage than an uncontrolled yield spike.
The late-session bond response therefore keeps the market from entering a more dangerous regime.
TOMORROW'S MICHIGAN REPORT BECOMES IMPORTANT
Friday brings the preliminary University of Michigan consumer survey.
The headline sentiment figure will matter.
But inflation expectations may matter more.
After this week's surge in oil, any meaningful increase in consumer inflation expectations could reinforce the bond market's concerns.
That would be particularly important if longer-term expectations move higher.
The market needs evidence that the energy shock is not becoming embedded.
THE OIL MARKET REMAINS TOMORROW'S FIRST SCREEN
Before analysing NQ Friday morning, traders should look at crude.
If Brent remains above $100 but stable or lower, the inflation impulse becomes easier to absorb.
If Brent begins accelerating towards fresh highs again, the entire rates problem can reappear quickly.
The current regime remains unusually sensitive to energy.
That makes oil a direct component of the NQ dashboard.
BULLISH SCENARIO — ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE: 48%
The bullish case has improved slightly from this morning because the Treasury auction was solid and yields moved away from their intraday extremes.
Oil also gave back part of the early surge.
For the bullish case to strengthen further, the 10Y needs to remain contained, Brent needs to stop accelerating and semiconductor breadth must improve.
The strongest confirmation would be:
10Y stable/down + oil stabilising + SOX recovery + NQ reclaiming lost ground + VIX contained.
That would indicate today's stress was absorbed rather than converted into a larger regime break.
BEARISH SCENARIO — ANALYTICAL ESTIMATE: 52%
The bearish case retains a slight edge.
Oil remains extremely elevated.
Long yields remain restrictive.
AI financing concerns are becoming more important.
Semiconductor breadth remains vulnerable.
And the market is increasingly competing with Treasury yields that offer historically attractive risk-free returns.
The strongest bearish confirmation would be:
Brent resumes higher + 10Y breaks above the recent stress zone + SOX weakens further + NQ loses the record-high structure.
That would shift the market from resilience into genuine valuation compression.
ANALYTICAL EDGE
BULLISH: 48%
BEARISH: 52%
EDGE: NEARLY NEUTRAL / SLIGHTLY BEARISH — MACRO PRESSURE REMAINS, BUT TREASURY DEMAND PREVENTED A WORSE OUTCOME.
This is an important change from the morning.
The risk backdrop is still difficult.
But the solid 30-year auction demonstrated that the Treasury market is not experiencing a demand vacuum.
That reduces one of the more extreme bearish risks.
The market remains under pressure.
It is not yet breaking.
CURRENT REGIME
CURRENT REGIME: NQ RESILIENCE UNDER OIL AND LONG-YIELD PRESSURE / SOLID TREASURY DEMAND / AI-FUNDING DEBATE / VALUATION COMPRESSION RISK.
The central message of Thursday is more nuanced than simply risk-off.
Oil shocked the market.
Yields remained high.
Semiconductors weakened.
AI financing concerns increased.
Yet the long-duration Treasury auction attracted buyers and NQ remained relatively close to record territory.
That is a stressed market.
It is not yet a broken one.
FINAL ANALYTICAL VIEW
Thursday may eventually prove to be one of the most important sessions of this week because it exposed the next stage of the AI-market debate.
The first stage was simple:
Is AI real?
The answer from revenues, chip demand and data-centre spending has increasingly been yes.
The second stage was:
Can AI earnings justify extremely high equity valuations?
The market has so far answered yes.
Now we are entering a third stage:
What does it cost to finance the infrastructure required to generate those earnings?
That question is fundamentally different.
If the AI cycle increasingly requires hundreds of billions of dollars of corporate debt, then technology is no longer merely a beneficiary of capital markets.
It becomes one of the largest competitors for capital.
That has implications for credit spreads, Treasury demand, corporate borrowing costs and ultimately the discount rate itself.
This creates a fascinating feedback loop:
AI growth increases earnings.
AI investment increases borrowing.
Borrowing can increase yields.
Higher yields reduce the present value of AI earnings.
That is the equation investors are beginning to price.
Today's solid 30-year auction is therefore genuinely important because it shows the system can still absorb enormous duration supply without immediately destabilising.
But it does not solve the larger issue.
Oil remains high.
Term premium remains high.
Long yields remain high.
AI borrowing is rising.
And equity valuations remain demanding.
So Friday's challenge is straightforward.
NQ no longer needs merely to prove that AI earnings are strong.
It needs to prove that those earnings can continue outrunning the rising cost of financing the entire AI ecosystem.
That may become the defining market question of the next phase.

California is home to about 2.3 million unauthorized immigrants, accounting for 20% of the national total and 6% of the state’s population as of 2019.

The majority of California’s illegal immigrants are from Mexico, but there are also sizable groups from Central America, Asia, and other regions.

California’s illegal immigrants are concentrated in the large coastal metropolitan areas, such as Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, and San Jose.
https://t.co/wa96Zp6S24

According to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), an estimated 2.6 million undocumented immigrants resided in California in 2022,

This represented the largest such population in any U.S. state, surpassing second-ranked Texas by more than half a million additional persons. The California number also represented 23.7 percent of the entire estimated undocumented immigrant population (11.99 million in 2022) in the United States. About 6.61 percent of California's population was estimated to be undocumented immigrants.

DHS has not offered undocumented immigrant estimates specifically for U.S. counties. The Migration Policy Institute, however, estimated the number in 2019, specifically in Los Angeles County, to have been 951,000 (see table below), almost 10 percent of the county's entire population and the highest concentration in any U.S. county.

The University of Southern California Center for the Study of Immigrant Integration reported that, in Los Angeles County, in 2016, 80 percent of undocumented persons were Latino, 10 percent were Asian or Pacific Islander, and 3 percent were white. It further reported that 68 percent of undocumented immigrants had lived in the United States for more than 10 years and that 852,000 U.S. citizen Angelenos and 273,000 legal permanent resident Angelenos lived with an undocumented family member. Combined with an estimated 886,000 Angelenos who were undocumented, that came to about 1 in 5 residents of Los Angeles County who were either undocumented or living with a family member who was undocumented.

American martial artist, kickboxer, and former multi-sport champion Fredia "The Cheetah" Gibbs walking down a hallway holding her International Sport Kickboxing Association (ISKA) world championship belt.... 

In 1993, a serial killer tried to rape a woman inside his van. He had no idea she was one of the most dangerous kickboxers in America.

Her name was Fredia Gibbs.

One night in Inglewood, California, Gibbs attended a domino game where she met a man named Lonnie Franklin Jr. When she began feeling strangely tired after accepting a drink from him, she decided to leave.

Franklin offered her a ride home.

She accepted.

But when Gibbs told him where to turn, he drove in the opposite direction. He eventually stopped in a secluded area and demanded sex.

Gibbs tried to open the door.

There was no handle.

She tried the window. That wouldn't open either.

According to Gibbs, Franklin had trapped her inside the van. When she refused his demands, he attempted to strike her.

She blocked the blow.

Then she fought back.

Gibbs had trained in martial arts since childhood and was already an undefeated professional kickboxer. She began throwing punches and powerful kicks, repeatedly striking Franklin's legs.

He tackled her, but she managed to overpower him, force him to the floor and demand the keys.

She unlocked the chained rear door, escaped into the darkness and eventually found a taxi.

Gibbs survived, but the experience left her deeply traumatized. She returned to Pennsylvania and initially refused to go back to California.

Then came an opportunity she had spent years preparing for.

In 1994, Gibbs defeated French champion Valérie Wiet-Henin in a stunning upset, becoming the first Black American woman to win an ISKA world kickboxing title. She eventually retired from kickboxing undefeated, with 16 victories and 15 knockouts.

But the identity of the man in the van would become clear only years later.

In 2010, Lonnie Franklin Jr. was arrested as the serial killer known as the Grim Sleeper. He was convicted in 2016 of murdering ten women and girls and attempting to murder another woman.

Gibbs has publicly identified Franklin as the man who attacked her that night in 1993. Her encounter was not part of his criminal conviction.

For years, she feared seeing him again.

The man who tried to overpower Fredia Gibbs had encountered a woman whose fighting skills were about to make history.

PROJECT STONE: CITY OF LIGHT SHINES ON THE PRIVATE LABYRINTH 

Olive Crest, the Public Land Agreement, the $810,000 Contract, and the California–Nevada Child-Welfare Accountability Trail

THE RECORDS EXIST. THE QUESTIONS ARE SPECIFIC. NOW FOLLOW EVERY AGREEMENT TO ITS FINAL PAYMENT AND EVERY REFERRAL TO ITS DOCUMENTED OUTCOME.

An investigative report by Project Stone | STONE-911 | WonderGrid

1. Start with the document that changes the investigation

I have been examining the relationships between child-welfare agencies, nonprofit providers, public funding, referrals, placements, and government oversight. I call this framework the PRIVATE LABYRINTH because responsibility can be distributed across institutions while the public struggles to see how the entire system works.

Now we have a specific Nevada government record that gives this investigation a concrete starting point.

On January 6, 2026, the Clark County Board of Commissioners approved agenda item 30, file 26-1054, authorizing a lease agreement between Clark County and Olive Crest. The property consists of approximately 113,266 square feet, or 2.6 acres, at Assessor’s Parcel Number 138-02-701-003, including the existing building at 4233 North Rancho Drive in Las Vegas. The county’s published staff report describes a proposed Children and Family Resource Center and 16 apartments intended to house at-risk young people who have aged out of foster care. Source: Clark County’s official agenda record.

Let us be precise about what that document says.

The proposed lease has a 25-year term with one additional 25-year option. The staff report states that Olive Crest would bear the costs of renovating the existing building, constructing future improvements, utilities, maintenance, repairs, staffing, and equipment. It also states that Clark County would receive first priority for up to 15% of available and unoccupied beds, subject to Olive Crest’s eligibility requirements.

And then there is the provision that deserves a closer financial examination.

THE COUNTY AGREED TO OFFER THE LEASE WITH NO RENT PAYMENT. Source: Clark County, file 26-1054.

That is not proof of corruption. It is a documented public-property arrangement that deserves to be understood in its entirety.

What is the market value of the property use? How was the no-rent arrangement evaluated? What public benefits did the county expect? What obligations become enforceable under the executed lease? How will the county determine whether the promised improvements and services are delivered?

Those questions can be answered with records.

The staff report lists the fiscal impact as not applicable, but it also explicitly states that the lease is offered without rent. That makes the valuation and approval rationale important audit questions. The report alone does not establish the dollar value of the rent foregone, and I will not invent one.

I WANT THE EXECUTED LEASE, THE PROPERTY VALUATION, THE APPROVAL MEMORANDUM, AND THE OVERSIGHT REQUIREMENTS.

I want the complete agreement, including exhibits, conditions, insurance requirements, reporting obligations, default provisions, termination rights, and any subsequent amendments. I want the actual parcel map and the documents showing what property was made available.

I want the county’s analysis of the public benefit and the financial assumptions behind the arrangement.

And I want to know what happens if the project is delayed, the apartments are never completed, the proposed services change, or the organization does not fulfill its contractual obligations.

A public announcement describes intentions. An executed agreement defines obligations. Inspection records, payment records, and performance reports show what actually happened.

That is where this investigation begins.
