text:
𝟕 𝐘𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐬 𝐋𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫: 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐔𝐧𝐭𝐨𝐥𝐝 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐨𝐟 𝐃𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐝 𝐓𝐫𝐮𝐦𝐩’𝐬 𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟗 𝐒𝐮𝐦𝐨 𝐕𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐭 (𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭 𝟏 𝐨𝐟 𝟐)
In May 2019, U.S. President Donald Trump visited Japan as the first state guest of the Reiwa era. Behind the realization of his sumo match attendance and the presentation of the United States President's Cup—an idea proposed by Prime Minister Abe—lay meticulous preparations where failure was not an option. Custom black leather slippers, temporary wooden stairs for the dohyo, and small phonetic symbols secretly added to the certificate to pronounce "Asanoyama"—.

From the book The Unknown World of American Diplomatic Protocol by Izumi Okubo, a protocol officer working for the U.S. Department of State, we present an excerpt revealing part of the untold behind-the-scenes struggles of the staff who fought to preserve the President's dignity and successfully execute the award ceremony.

𝘖𝘳𝘪𝘨𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘭 𝘢𝘳𝘵𝘪𝘤𝘭𝘦 𝘧𝘳𝘰𝘮 𝘉𝘶𝘯𝘴𝘩𝘶𝘯, 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘭𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘣𝘺 𝘐𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘢𝘯𝘰𝘻𝘦𝘬𝘪. 𝘗𝘢𝘳𝘵 1 𝘰𝘳 2.

𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐓𝐫𝐮𝐦𝐩’𝐬 𝐕𝐢𝐬𝐢𝐭 𝐚𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐆𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐢𝐰𝐚 𝐄𝐫𝐚
In May of the first year of Reiwa (2019), President Donald Trump and the First Lady visited Japan for the second time, following their 2017 trip, becoming the first foreign state guests welcomed after the Emperor's accession to the throne. Among the itinerary, which included a State Banquet at the Imperial Palace, attending the final day of the May Grand Sumo Tournament required a truly unique set of preparations. As explained to us, this outing was incorporated at the personal direction of Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, who wanted President and Mrs. Trump to experience traditional Japanese culture firsthand.

In the championship presentation ceremony held after all the bouts were completed, the presentation of the U.S. President's Cup was scheduled right after Prime Minister Abe's presentation of the Prime Minister's Cup. Hosting the President at a packed, square-shaped Ryogoku Kokugikan required meticulous coordination regarding security, safety, and movement flow. Managing these adjustments became the job of the advance team.

When I visited Ryogoku Kokugikan for the first time on a site visit as part of the advance team, I received an explanation of the rough movement routes after arrival and a few candidate locations from which they could watch the matches. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs explained that Prime Minister Abe strongly wished for the President to experience the full excitement of Japanese sumo as much as possible, suggesting a seat in the ingside seats as one candidate. Box seats were also proposed as options, so we brought these ideas back to evaluate.

Ultimately, the decision was made to install VIP seating by modifying a section of the box seats. Normally, sitting directly on the tatami floor in Masuseki is standard in Japan, but Americans do not have a habit of sitting on the floor. As a compromise, it was proposed to prepare custom chairs for the Presidential and Prime Minister couples and install them inside the box seat area. Although slightly different from Japanese tradition, this seating arrangement was reached by mutual respect for each other’s culture and customs.

𝐒𝐮𝐩𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐛𝐲 𝐊𝐚𝐬𝐮𝐠𝐚𝐧𝐨 𝐎𝐲𝐚𝐤𝐚𝐭𝐚: "𝐁𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐇𝐢𝐬 𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐈𝐬 𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭’𝐬"
The Kokugikan is constructed in a bowl shape, with spectator seating fanning out in all four directions around the ring. Although seats higher up are stepped, because other spectators were sitting on the floor, installing chairs required careful consideration so as not to obstruct the view of those behind them. Furthermore, because box seats are partitioned by iron railings, we had to adjust the chair height so that the backs of their knees wouldn't hit the front railing and the soles of their feet would rest comfortably on the floor.

During these adjustments, in addition to an American staff member who had a similar height and leg length to the President, we received invaluable assistance from Kasugano Oyakata. Saying, "My build is close to the President's," he sat in the chair repeatedly to verify its width, knee angle, and ease of standing up. He also shared detailed feedback on whether the sitting posture looked natural and whether standing up to transition to the award ceremony would look awkward. Watching this process unfold in a venue surrounded by cameras on all four sides, I felt once again that trying to stand up directly from a tatami floor might cause someone to lose their balance, and choosing to install chairs was indeed the right decision.

Once the seating was finalized, the next step was confirming the order of the award ceremony and the associated movement routes. These site visits were repeated at the Kokugikan every day after 6:00 PM, when the final bout ended, until the day of the actual event. We split into setup/protocol teams and security teams, working out the fine details of our respective specialties. As part of the setup team, I primarily participated in verifying the President's movement routes.

Rehearsals for the award ceremony itself were also necessary. For the ceremony, who would be on the ring, and where would they wait? At what timing would the President step onto the ring, where would he stop, at what angle would he read the certificate, and how would he lift and hand over the trophy?

In sync with simulated real-time announcements provided by the Sumo Association, staff playing the role of the President repeatedly rehearsed the sequence—stepping onto the ring, reading the certificate, and presenting the President's Cup—eliminating any unnecessary movement. To help the President visually grasp this sequence of actions, an aide in charge of explaining the process played the role of the President to demonstrate the ceremony's flow, which was filmed on a smartphone to create an instructional video. These walkthroughs and preparations progressed with the cooperation of the Sumo Association, and I served as an interpreter responsible for explaining posture and movement details.

𝐁𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐋𝐞𝐚𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐒𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐓𝐞𝐦𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐫𝐲 𝐖𝐨𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐧 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐫𝐬
Around the sumo ring, there was another sacred, unbreakable rule: the strict prohibition of women entering the ring. The ring is considered sacred ground, and items such as dried squid, kelp, washed rice, salt, dried chestnuts, and nutmeg seeds are buried in the center as shizumemono (sacred offerings). Because it is a sacred place based on ancient tradition, women touching the ring was also something to be avoided.

As the interpreter confirming movement routes, I stood beside a microphone stand placed a short distance from the edge of the ring, using hand gestures to communicate movements to the American staff member playing "the President." Every time I moved slightly, members of the Sumo Association and colleagues from the U.S. Embassy repeatedly called out, "Don't stumble!" This was because any situation where the ring was damaged and needed rebuilding during the May Tournament had to be avoided at all costs.

From these site visit walkthroughs, several "issues to address" emerged.

Shoes are strictly forbidden on the sumo ring. However, in America, there is virtually no habit of taking off one's shoes in public. Furthermore, removing socks to go barefoot is a relaxed gesture done at home, not the protocol for a U.S. President at an official event.

Therefore, we discussed footwear with the Sumo Association for when the President would step onto the ring to present the trophy during the award ceremony. While wrestlers are naturally barefoot, there were precedents for suit-attired guests wearing slippers, which the Sumo Association offered to provide. However, they did not have "extra-large" slippers that would fit the President's feet. Consequently, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs arranged to procure black leather slippers from the United States for Prime Minister Abe and President Trump.

Furthermore, the advance team unanimously agreed that the step used to climb onto the ring required a creative solution. In sumo, the shallow cutouts on the side of the ring are normally used as steps, but the tread is narrow, and climbing them stably requires practice. Under the watchful eyes of a full crowd and press cameras, the President could not afford to stumble while stepping onto the ring. Therefore, on this day, temporary wooden stairs were installed beside the ring, providing a wide tread for each step. This, too, was behind-the-scenes preparation aimed at making a leader look like a leader.

(𝘦𝘯𝘥 𝘰𝘧 𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘵 1 𝘰𝘧 2)

Tomorrow, Saturday, 10 October 2026, is Mahalaya Amavasya, also called Sarva Pitru Amavasya. It is the final day of Pitru Paksha and is observed for all ancestors, including those whose shraddha tithi is unknown or was Tomorrow is very auspicious day for our Ancestors.

The Amavasya tithi begins late on 9 October (around 9:35 pm) and ends on 10 October evening (around 9:19 pm), so the main rituals fall on the 10th. Tarpan, shraddha and pind daan are traditionally offered in the daytime, especially during Kutup, Rohina and Aparahna, with water, black sesame and kusha, facing south.

The day is also the farewell of the pitrs and the threshold of Devi Paksha. In the evening, darshan of Bhagwati in the temple is considered auspicious as Sharadiya Navratri begins the next day.

text:
On April 3, 2019, Doris Day turned 97 and chose to spend the day in the quiet of her Carmel Valley home, surrounded not by grandeur, but by handwritten letters, printed emails, and cards sent from fans across the world. Her longtime friend and publicist, Bob Bashara, recalled how she sat near her window that morning, sunlight streaming through the lace curtains, holding a magnifying glass in one hand and a letter in the other. Each message, whether from someone who remembered her radiant smile in "Calamity Jane" or someone who had only recently discovered her voice through "Que Sera, Sera," was opened and read with care.

“She insisted on reading every single one,” Bashara said in a soft interview with "People" magazine. “She kept saying, ‘These people stayed with me all these years. I need them to know I’m still here, and I hear them.’” There was no fanfare that day, no camera crew, no social media announcements. It was the purest form of gratitude, an aging star acknowledging the people who had never stopped loving her.

That morning, a letter came from a 72-year-old woman in Michigan who had grown up listening to Doris’s songs on her grandmother’s radio. In it, she wrote, “Your voice comforted me when my parents divorced. Your films made me laugh through college heartbreaks. You don’t know me, but you’ve lived in my heart.” Doris paused as she read those words aloud, eyes misting. Then she set the letter down and whispered, “I know her now.”

Another envelope, addressed with careful calligraphy, had traveled from Japan. A young pianist in Tokyo shared how "Secret Love" inspired him to start composing. Doris smiled gently and asked Bashara to reply with a thank-you note and a signed photograph, one of the few she had left in a drawer by the desk.
Though her health had declined in recent years, Doris refused to speak of pain or limitations. She never complained. Her joy that day came from being remembered not as a movie star, but as a person who had brought something kind into others’ lives. Her assistant noticed that Doris kept a small notebook beside her, jotting names and little notes as she read each message. “She didn’t want anyone to feel like they were forgotten,” the assistant later said.
She had chosen solitude for her birthday that year, turning down offers for interviews and appearances. What mattered most to her, according to those closest, was that fans knew she still cared. And she did. She had always said that fame was never the point, it was the connection. “She believed her success belonged to the people who supported her, not to herself,” Bashara added in his conversation with "The Hollywood Reporter."
Five weeks later, on May 13, 2019, Doris Day passed away peacefully at her home from complications related to pneumonia. No public funeral was held, as per her wishes. Her ashes were scattered privately, and her Carmel home was soon put up for sale. But the spirit of that last birthday lingered, an image of a woman in her 90s, sitting quietly with letters of love from strangers she considered friends.

That final birthday was not marked by applause, lights, or tribute specials. It was spent with ink on paper, with emotions running through cursive handwriting, with memories folded into envelopes. It was a day of receiving and giving, one last exchange of affection from a woman who had spent her entire life offering her heart to the world. She spent her last birthday exactly as she had lived, gracious, warm, and deeply connected to the people who loved her.

text:
Is Mediocrity The New Norm
by Greg Allen
Published Jul 15, 2012 

Stockton, California recently filed bankruptcy.  It’s the largest city in US history to do so.  The mayor of Scranton, Pennsylvania recently declared his town’s broke too.  The mayor felt he had little choice but to take drastic measures to offset their devastating 16.8 million dollar shortfall.  Since the city can’t pay its bills, the mayor proclaimed he and every city employee would have their compensation slashed to the minimum wage of $7.25 an hour.

Is that the new norm we’re faced with?

84,000 US jobs were created in the month of June, but 85,000 individuals went on Social Security disability at the same time.  Many of the unemployed are finding out there are no jobs to be had and when their 99 weeks of unemployment compensation runs out, they file for disability.

8 million Americans are on Social Security disability and a record 45 million are on food stamps.

Is that the new lowly norm?

Public perception used to be it was shameful to be on welfare and food stamps – is mediocrity now the norm?

Many have said Barack Obama is “scary.”  Name one president, you can recall, who’s been labeled that?  I can think of several presidents who were defined by many things, but never one who was considered to be frightening.

One can only surmise what President Obama will go down in history as, but will a label of the food stamp president, or a deficit shattering spendthrift ever stick?

Is a mediocre pursuit of happiness the new norm for America?

Is trifleness the new norm when it comes to education as well?  Is it to be expected that half of all college grads can’t find work even though they’ve spent thousands of dollars, and went in debt to do so, to obtain a degree that may or may not suffice anymore?

What does it say about our culture when Rutgers University offers a course in “Underwater basket weaving,” that Montclair State University offers a class titled “How to watch television,” or that Occidental College offers credits for attending a course called “Stupidity?”

Society has fallen prey to a progressively bent logic, which isn’t really progressive at all but regressive, that says everyone gets a trophy.  To say all children must be dealt the same rewards, that none should suffer any measure of sensory failure, is a damning venture that has caused more harm than good.

When my brother’s stepson was young, he would constantly say: “I’m special, cause grandma says so!”  He may be well thought of by those close to him, but an insurmountable many more don’t see it that way.

I’m sure many have failed to recognize the socialist plight that has plagued us.  In reality, not all are the same.  There can only be one Super Bowl winner in a given year, one World Series champion, or one NBA winner crowned.

Society now suffers from the entitlement syndrome our children were taught.  Many kids think once they get out of college a well-paying job is just waiting for them, but that couldn’t be farther from the truth.

For many Americans, it’s not in their DNA to do just enough to get by.  Yet, for many more they see life as mediocre at best and the entitlement stigma they feel they deserve has attached itself.  For many, to just exist in life is fine and it can become a reality if they only relent to the entangling dependence government offers.

With the results we’re seeing manifested in Washington, D.C. one can only conclude that mediocrity is the new norm – if that’s so, the American dream is dead.  However, I believe there are scores of those who won’t allow that idealization of what America is to just wither.

The American dream imparts that hard work and determination isn’t some novelty and success can be accomplished by anyone.  Pride resides in many across the land and to have a President whose ideology isn’t that is a notion that will be pushed back by a majority who do believe in a dream.

America is truly an astonishing place and although she may have lost her way that fair Lady has by no means doused that flame of liberty in a muddied pond of hopelessness.

Greg Allen’s column, Thinkin’ Out Loud, was published bi-monthly from 2009 to 2017.  He’s an author, a former nationally syndicated columnist and the founder of Builder of the Spirit Ministries in Jamestown, Indiana.  He can be reached at https://t.co/9QdchPfdBy.

This video shows the moment Mark Zuckerberg got into Harvard in 2002. Two years later, he dropped out to build Facebook with just $85 in his pocket

"Dad, I always told you I'd come back and get my degree"

In the video, teenage Mark sits at an old computer in his pajama pants while his dad films. When Mark reads "accepted," his dad jokes that even the family dog is now part of "Harvard's class of 2006"

At Harvard he built websites in his dorm room. One of them, Facemash, got shut down within days and landed him in front of the disciplinary board

On February 4, 2004, he launched TheFacebook from the same dorm. Within a month, more than half of Harvard had signed up. That summer he moved to California and never went back to class

At first glance, only a fool leaves one of the best colleges in the world to bet everything on a website

But Mark had done it before. In high school, Microsoft and AOL wanted to buy his music app and hire him. He said no and went to Harvard

At 22, Yahoo offered him $1 billion for Facebook. He said no again

Today about 3 billion people use Facebook every month

In 2017, Harvard invited him back to give the graduation speech and gave him an honorary degree. That's where he said the line to his dad. The man who held the camera was in the crowd

Would you drop out of Harvard for a website you built in your dorm room, or stay and finish your degree?

Of the men inside Fort Sumter in April 1861, only one came from a state that would soon join the Confederacy and then followed it. Second Lieutenant Richard Kidder Meade of the Corps of Engineers, West Point class of 1857 and a native of the Petersburg area, had helped move Major Robert Anderson’s garrison from Fort Moultrie to Sumter in December 1860. He refused a South Carolina demand to surrender Castle Pinckney, stayed with the fort through the bombardment of April 12–13, and only afterward moved to the CSA ranks because of his state’s decision. Virginia’s convention voted to secede on April 17; Meade resigned his U.S. commission, accepted about May 1, and entered Confederate service as a major of engineers. He later worked on the fortifications at Fort Fisher and died of typhoid in 1862.

He was also the grandson of a man who had ridden for George Washington. Lieutenant Colonel Richard Kidder Meade, a Virginian educated in England, was appointed one of Washington’s aides-de-camp in March 1777 and served through the Philadelphia campaign, Valley Forge, and Monmouth. His son, also Richard Kidder Meade, became a Virginia congressman and U.S. minister to Brazil; that man’s son was the engineer at Sumter. Like Robert E. Lee, he did not leave the United States Army when the first Deep South states seceded. He stood to his post through the bombardment, and only after Virginia herself left the Union did he resign and offer his sword to his state. Nobody in their right mind would say his views ln the subject of slavery changed. Everyone understood that duty dictated the actions of Meade.

Abbas later said he rejected it because he was not left a copy of the map. 

Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat confirmed the offer and the refusal in a March 2009 Al Jazeera interview.

PUTIN'S 74TH BIRTHDAY: BURNING OIL, DISPUTED VICTORIES AND A CASCADE OF SCANDALS 🇷🇺🇺🇦

Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday was accompanied by a remarkable collection of reported incidents across Russia, from an oil tanker fire off Sochi to allegations of fabricated battlefield footage, military desertions, corruption and a deadly laboratory accident.

Off the Black Sea resort city of Sochi, an oil tanker reportedly exploded, sending flames and thick smoke into the air near luxury beachfront properties. According to accounts circulating online, Russian authorities took approximately three hours to respond publicly, eventually restricting access to the coastline and instructing residents to keep their windows closed. Officials nevertheless claimed that air pollution remained well below legal limits.

Former Ukrainian politician and pro-Russian commentator Oleg Tsarev reportedly anticipated that Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratyev would attribute the fire to falling debris. Ukrainian channels, meanwhile, mocked the incident with references to sightseeing tours of a burning Sochi.

At the same time, Russia's Defense Ministry announced the purported capture of Holubkove. However, geolocation analysts challenged the announcement, alleging that the accompanying footage had been recorded in August and digitally altered to display a Russian flag. The authenticity and timing of the video remain disputed.

Other reports painted a troubling picture of conditions within Russian forces. Nearly 1,000 personnel from units associated with Red Square parades were reportedly recorded as deserters in a single sector. One pro-war blogger seeking donations for urgently needed drone equipment allegedly collected just 1,200 rubles, approximately $13.

Around Lyman, Russian military channels described improvements in the situation despite reports that Russian defensive positions had withdrawn behind a river while Ukrainian forces crossed along both banks. Separately, St. Petersburg reportedly reduced volunteer enlistment bonuses by two-thirds, coinciding with the enlistment of a State Duma deputy.

Beyond the battlefield, an especially serious allegation emerged from the Irkutsk region. According to the account, 28-year-old laboratory technician Darya Shipilova died after accidentally breaking a test tube containing a pneumonic plague pathogen. The account further alleges that Moscow rejected an American 🇺🇸 offer of medical assistance and responded by offering help with measles.

It also claims that, when the World Health Organization sought clarification, Russian officials denied any recorded case in Irkutsk itself, while Shipilova had reportedly died in nearby Shelekhov. These allegations, including the reported laboratory exposure and official response, require independent verification.

Tensions involving NATO countries featured in the same series of reports. Lithuania 🇱🇹 was said to have voted to remove restrictions concerning weapons of mass destruction, prompting Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov to warn against NATO nuclear deployments near Russia. The account contrasted that warning with Russia's own nuclear weapons deployment arrangements in Belarus 🇧🇾.

In Finland 🇫🇮, an extraordinary allegation claimed that Russian intelligence operatives had entered lawmakers' homes and deliberately contaminated their toilets as an intimidation tactic. The account compared this with a separate alleged incident involving the luggage of a senior American official in 2023. Neither allegation is established by the material provided.

Corruption allegations also resurfaced around Patriot Park, Russia's military-themed complex near Moscow. The account reports the arrest of Igor Vasilyev over an alleged 80-million-ruble bribe, describing him as the twelfth official implicated in investigations connected to the facility.

As Ukraine's General Staff condemned Putin's legacy, the Kremlin emphasized personal birthday greetings. North Korean 🇰🇵 leader Kim Jong Un reportedly sent a message reaffirming his personal commitment to the Russian president.

Taken together, the incidents presented in this account offer a striking contrast between the Kremlin's carefully managed public messaging and allegations of serious problems involving military operations, internal security, public health and corruption.

Several of the more extraordinary claims remain unverified, and the individual reports should not be treated as established facts without further corroboration.

text:
Jezus and some ideas that later became "socialism "

What follows is a top 10 of ideas often called socialist, each paired with a saying attributed to him (or, where noted, to the earliest community that claimed him). Quotes are standard English renderings of the Gospels and Acts.
Shared goods, not private hoarding. The earliest Jesus movement is described as holding property in common. “All the believers were together and had everything in common. They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need” (Acts 2:44–45; also Acts 4:32–35). That is voluntary community practice, not a state taking the means of production.
Liquidate wealth for the poor. To a rich man who asked about eternal life: “Go, sell everything you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me” (Mark 10:21; Matthew 19:21; Luke 18:22). The man walks away. The demand is personal discipleship, not a tax code.
Wealth as a spiritual obstacle. “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God… It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of God” (Mark 10:23–25). The point is attachment, not a wealth ceiling enforced by law.
Blessing aimed at the poor. “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God… But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort” (Luke 6:20, 24). Matthew’s version says “poor in spirit.” Luke is blunter about material poverty.
Judgment by treatment of the needy. “I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in… whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me” (Matthew 25:35–40). Failure is pictured as eternal loss. The actors are individuals and nations in a parable, not a planning ministry.
You cannot serve God and money. “No one can serve two masters… You cannot serve both God and money” (Matthew 6:24). Greed is treated as idolatry, not as a property form to be nationalized.
Do not store surplus for yourself. “Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth… But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven” (Matthew 6:19–20). The rich fool who builds bigger barns is called a fool because he dies that night (Luke 12:16–21). The alternative offered is “Sell your possessions and give to the poor” (Luke 12:33).
The rich man and the beggar. In the parable, a rich man feasts while Lazarus starves at his gate; after death their places reverse (Luke 16:19–31). No policy mechanism is described. The warning is about indifference.
Pay workers what is due. Day laborers in the vineyard are paid a full denarius even if hired late; the owner says the wage is his to set and that he is generous (Matthew 20:1–16). It is not equal pay for equal work. It is an argument about grace. Separately, withholding wages is condemned in the tradition around him (James 5:4, not a Jesus saying).
Care for the outsider and the debtor. Love of neighbor and of enemy (Matthew 5:43–44; Luke 10:25–37, the Samaritan), forgiveness of debts in the Lord’s Prayer (“forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors,” Matthew 6:12), and the Jubilee-style language he applies to himself in Luke 4:18–19 (good news to the poor, freedom for prisoners, the year of the Lord’s favor). These are moral and religious commands.

Minerva Morning Update
10/9/2026

Friday Morning Mish-Mash

No single thread. Thursday was an AI-revenue scare that hit the complex hard — Nasdaq −1.25% to 27,193, S&P −0.47% to 7,765, SOX −3.4% — and Friday’s open is a partial unwind plus two discrete catalysts that actually change positioning: SpaceX buying its way into the carrier stack, and Lumentum saying the optical book is sold out through early 2029. Oil is slipping after Trump pushed any Iran strike past the Nov. 3 midterms. Futures: Nasdaq +0.7–0.8%, S&P +0.4%, Dow flat to +0.1%. Indexes were still on track for slim weekly gains into the print. Banks and CPI next week. Don’t force a thesis.

★ MOST ACTIONABLE · $SPCX $T $VZ $TMUS $AMT $CCI $SBAC

SpaceX Buys the 800 MHz Book — Starlink Mobile as a Fourth Carrier

SpaceX agreed to buy Grain Management’s nationwide 800 MHz portfolio, about $8 billion cash per the WSJ, subject to FCC approval. Up to 14 MHz of paired low-band. The point of the band is indoor penetration — walls and tree cover — which mid-band 2 GHz direct-to-cell does not do. SpaceX’s line: with this plus the Gen2 constellation (FCC cleared 15,000 V2 satellites this week, company claims >100x current bandwidth), Starlink Mobile becomes a major US carrier, satellite plus terrestrial, not a dead-zone add-on. Musk: “complete phone coverage in America.”

Tape: SPCX +3.7% premarket. TMUS and T −6% to −7.5%, VZ −5.3%. Towers the other side — AMT, CCI, SBAC +7–8%. Grain had only just taken this book off T-Mobile in August for cash plus 600 MHz. Verizon’s response is the bear case in one line: spectrum without a terrestrial network is empty airwaves. Capacity in dense urban cores is the open question; New Street-type framing is that a Starlink broadband + mobile bundle (Grok in the package is the xAI kicker being floated) is the real product, not a like-for-like replacement of macro RAN on day one.

Swing read: this is a narrative shock, not a completed network. Incumbent multiple compression can run for days while the FCC clock and build economics get debated. Towers are the hedge — more nodes if Starlink densifies, or a relative-safety bid if the market decides the moat just cracked. EchoStar (ECHO +4%) is the prior spectrum seller sitting in the same complex.

★ MOST ACTIONABLE · ▲ POSITIVE · $LITE $COHR $AAOI $CIEN

Optics: Sold Out Through Early 2029

Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston, Tokyo, Friday: optical components “completely sold out” through early 2029. Cannot meet ~70% of demand for some products through next year; still short ~30% of demand on others through 2028. Six months ago the sell-out date he was using was 2028. “We are very, very far behind what customers want… no end in sight.” Nvidia put $2 billion into LITE and $2 billion into Coherent earlier this year. Street expects Lumentum sales to more than double this year.

Premarket: LITE +6%, COHR +5%, with CIEN / AAOI / GLW bid. This is the reversal of Thursday’s optical dump — COHR −9.6%, GLW −6.4%, LITE −5.6% — which was the OpenAI-revenue contagion, not a demand print. FinTwit will treat Hurlston as the clean rebuttal to the “AI capex air pocket” story. It is a supply comment, not a margin or pricing comment. Chase risk is real after a 180%+ YTD on LITE.

OpenAI: The $50B Scare, Then the $70B Walk-Back

What hit the tape Thursday: FT / Bloomberg — annualized revenue ~$50 billion at end of September, vs. the ~$70 billion figure that had been circulating. Enterprise run-rate +107% in Q3, total +77%, per a person familiar cited by CNBC. Anthropic was already through ~$65 billion annualized at end of July, which is why the comparison stung.

What repaired it overnight: Bloomberg — OpenAI told investors it expects to reach or exceed $70 billion annualized by year-end, enterprise-led. NVDA and AMD +~1.7% premarket, AVGO +2.1%. Roundhill DRAM and SOXX +~2%. Thursday damage: NVDA −2.9%, AMD −3.9%, AVGO −4.4%, MU −4.8%, SNDK −4.9%, ORCL −5.5%, INTC −5.3%.

Expert split worth keeping: Bloomberg Intelligence’s Mandeep Singh — revenue-accounting noise, token growth still says infrastructure demand is intact. The bear camp (and Thursday’s price) says a $20 billion hole versus the number the Street was underwriting is exactly how circular-financing anxiety gets a bid. Both can be true for a few sessions. Memory does not get the same overnight absolution optics just got.

▼ NEGATIVE · $AAPL

Apple Cuts iPhone 18 Pro Orders

Nikkei: Apple told suppliers to cut component orders for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max. Memory inflation forced price hikes; premium uptake is softer than the build plan. AAPL −2%+ premarket. This is the other side of the MU / SNDK tape — hyperscaler LTAs win, the handset OEM eats BOM or cuts units. Gross-margin story at the flagship, not a volume story, and the order cut says they are choosing units down over full pass-through.

Offset, not a savior: Bloomberg says a first touchscreen MacBook and a new iPad mini around Oct. 27, plus 14-inch MacBook Pro and iMac on M6, OLED, lighter Pros, Dynamic Island on the Mac. A product event is a headline; it does not fix a Pro-cycle build cut.

★ MOST ACTIONABLE · ▲ $HUM · ▼ $ALHC

CMS 2027 Stars — Bonus Money Just Got Allocated

Humana: 95% of Medicare Advantage members in 4.0-star-or-better plans for 2027; 42% in 4.5-star. HUM +15–16% premarket. That is the quality-bonus pool reopening. Alignment Healthcare: a 2027 plan at 3.5 stars, ALHC −20%+. Aetna (CVS): more than 69% of MA members in 4-star-or-better. Clover (CLOV) +10% in sympathy.

Stars are a multi-quarter payment event, not a one-day gap. The trade is the gap versus the bonus math — HUM’s rerating can extend if the 4.5-star cohort is big enough to move 2027 revenue; ALHC is a broken-rating story until management shows a path back to 4.0. Managed care was already a relative hideout while AI de-grossed on Thursday.

▼ NEGATIVE · $DAL · ▲ $VLO $MPC

Delta Misses and Cuts — Fuel Is the P&L

DAL Q3 adj. EPS $1.72 vs. $1.89, revenue $17.59B vs. $17.66B. Full-year adj. EPS cut to $5.10–$5.60 from $6.50–$7.50 in July. Midpoint $5.35 sits under the $5.46 consensus. Annual fuel bill seen ~$6 billion higher than last year. Stock −3%. Demand in the premium cabin is fine; the barrel is not.

Refiners are the long side of the same fact. WSJ this morning: VLO, MPC, PSX set to crush already-strong June-quarter results as wars shrink product supply. Thursday tape already knew — MPC +4.8%, VLO +4.6%. Gulf product exports still estimated around half of pre-war levels. Distillate tightness is the structural piece; the flat price is the tradeable piece.

Macro: Oil Pause, Fed Still Leaning Higher

Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the midterms. WTI ~$90.50 (−1%), Brent ~$103 (−1.4%), off Thursday’s spike (WTI +3.6%, Brent +4.1%, Brent through $104–106 intraday on strike chatter and Hormuz tanker noise). A three-week geopolitical pause is not a supply fix. Hurricane risk still sits on Gulf output.

Fed: policy is 3.75–4.00% after Warsh’s September hike, the first in three years. Musalem Thursday: more firming required, another hike inside six to nine months if you want 2% inside ~18 months. Waller: more hikes likely, but not necessarily consecutive — October pause is open. Minutes: most participants saw another hike by year-end; several say current policy is not restrictive. Futures: October hold the base case (meeting is Oct. 27–28, a week before the election), December still live. 10-year around 5.25%. Today: Michigan sentiment and inflation expectations at 10:00 ET, WASDE at noon, rigs at 1:00 ET.

Analyst Desk

Barclays reshuffled eVTOL overnight: ACHR to Overweight, target $8 from $4.50; EVTL to Equal Weight from Underweight; JOBY to Underweight. A pair trade inside a group the market still treats as a narrative, not a certification calendar.

Morgan Stanley: CBOE to Overweight from Underweight, target $358 from $258 — S&P contract renewal removes the overhang, KPI contracts seen as upside outside the model. GEMI to Underweight, target $4.75 from $5.50 — crypto beta does not fix scale or a path to profitable growth.

JPMorgan: VFC to Neutral from Underweight, target $18 unchanged. KBW cut GNW and VOYA to Market Perform.

Also on the Wire

Samsung is the first tech name to forecast quarterly operating profit above ₩100 trillion (~$74.7 billion). Supportive for the memory-shortage narrative even after US memory was offered on Thursday. Do not confuse a Korean print with a US multiple.

PepsiCo beat on Thursday and was a rare large-cap green print in a red tape. Not a sector call.

RTX: $6.34 billion Standard Missile-3 production award. KOPN: additional $18.6 million US Army contract. Defense bid is idiosyncratic, not a group day.

Canada unemployment 6.5% in September. A small read-through for North American cyclicals, not a US print.

VEEA +40%+ on regained Nasdaq compliance after a reverse split and board cleanup. Micro-cap listing repair, not a signal.

Next week is the real earnings card: big banks Tuesday onward, CPI in the same window. Thursday’s software bounce (CSGP +8%, GDDY and ACN +6%) was a de-grossing of AI beta into “cheap quality,” not a fundamental reset. If the OpenAI walk-back holds through the cash open, that rotation can give some back.

NFA. DYOR. Not investment advice. Catalysts cut both ways; size for the gap, not the headline.

text:
Back in the day:

Major John André was a British officer who met Benedict Arnold and carried the papers for the plot to hand over West Point to the Brits.

André was captured near Tarrytown, New York, on September 23, 1780, out of uniform and using a false name, with the West Point plans hidden in his boot. A board of American officers convened by Washington found him a spy and sentenced him to death. He asked Washington to be shot as a soldier rather than hanged as a spy. That request was refused, and no answer was sent. Washington also offered to exchange him for Arnold; the British would not give Arnold up.

He was hanged at noon on October 2, 1780, at Tappan, New York, in front of the Continental Army camp. Accounts put the crowd in the thousands, mostly troops, and local people later filed past the body. His last words were that those present should bear witness he met his fate as a brave soldier.

We present the story “The Nerves of War and the Fender of Love” — about Commander “Timso,” military communications, and the human warmth that survives on the front lines.

Communications in war are not a “convenience.” Coordination, timely assistance, and the lives of fighters depend on them. That is why the knowledge, attentiveness, and high standards of those responsible for communications are especially important here.

One of the story’s protagonists is “Timso,” a commander in the “Akhmat” Special Forces detachment. The author portrays him not only while carrying out missions but also in everyday interactions, through his speech, humor, and attitude toward people. text:
The United States is gearing up to livestream a military firing squad—a stark contrast to Britain and other countries, which protect children from such graphic images differently. On December 3, the Pentagon plans to execute Nidal Hasan, the former Army major convicted of the 2009 Fort Hood shootings, by firing squad at 1 p.m. Central. Pete Hegseth has publicly said this chilling event should be accessible to viewers, and officials confirm they will livestream it. This would mark the first U.S. military execution since 1961 and the first public execution in the country since the 1930s.

In the UK, protective measures like Ofcom’s watershed ensure that material potentially harmful to under-18s isn’t broadcast before 9 p.m., with the most violent content scheduled for even later slots. A broadcast execution would not be planned for daytime and would likely be blocked altogether.

The U.S. has no such equivalent. The FCC’s 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. restrictions address indecency and profanity—sexual or excretory content—not graphic violence. Violence is largely regulated through voluntary ratings and the V-chip. Cable and streaming platforms operate outside these rules. Because a Pentagon livestream isn’t considered an FCC broadcast, safe-harbour hours don’t apply. Current U.S. laws offer no safeguards against a 1 p.m. livestream that could reach children online.

A stark contrast: one country shields its youth with strict timing rules; the other leaves it exposed to streaming violence anytime, anywhere.

✝️ God Begins to Fulfill His Promises

1. God always keeps His promises. No matter how impossible it seems, or how long it may take, every one of His promises will come true.

2. God gave a son to Zacharias and Elisabeth, even though they were very old. They named him John, as God had told them. (Lk. 1:57)

3. Zacharias believed in God’s promise to send a Savior, Who would save the world from the power of sin and Satan. The Spirit of God told him that the Savior would come very soon. The promised “seed of the woman”, the “seed of Abraham”, was about to be born. John would be the prophet to prepare the way for the coming of the Savior, “the Lord”. (Lk. 1:67-79, Gen. 3:15, Gen. 12:3)

4. God Himself is the great Savior. He saved Noah from the flood, Isaac from the sacrifice, Lot from Sodom, and Joseph from prison. He saved Israel from slavery in Egypt, from Pharaoh’s army at the Red Sea, and from death in the wilderness. (Is. 43:11)

5. People like to think that they are strong, wise, and in control. Satan wants us to be confident in ourselves. The unpleasant truth is that we are all sinners, hopelessly lost and unable to save ourselves. We are condemned to everlasting punishment in Hell. We need a Savior that will rescue us from our sin.

6. Zacharias prophesied that the Savior would come as the sunrise to us, who are in darkness, and would guide us to the way of peace and forgiveness of sin. He would give us the light so that we could see the way of Salvation. When you are lost, the light can show you where you are, and which way you need to go. Just as there is only one sun, there is only one Savior. (Lk. 1:77-79)

7. John lived in the desert until it was time for him to begin preaching. He was a sinful man, but he believed God, and trusted in the promise of a coming savior. It would be his job to tell the people that the Savior had finally come. (Lk. 1:80)

8. Jesus, the coming Savior, had to meet many qualifications in order to fulfill all the promises that God had made for 4000 years. He had to be a descendant of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and David. 
He had to fit all the descriptions of the prophets.

9. Many of the prophecies in the Old Testament had double meanings. They were talking about something that happened back then, but they also had a message about something that would happen in the future. Often it was not clear exactly what would happen, but after it happened, you could clearly see how God had foretold it in the prophecies. Sometimes the prophets themselves did not completely understand what they were writing about. They just wrote the words that God gave them. (1Pet. 1:10-12)

10. Hundreds of years before Jesus was born, the prophets told many things about what He would be like, what He would do, and what would happen to Him. Every one of these details came to pass.

11. Jesus is also called “the Christ”, which means “the anointed One”. This means He was specially chosen by God to perform a certain mission. Another form of this same name is “the Messiah”.

12. As the Messiah, Jesus has three special roles in God’s plan of salvation. He is a prophet, who came to tell us the way of Salvation from sin, Satan, and Hell. He is a priest, who offered the blood of the sacrifice as a payment for sin. He is a king, who will someday rule over all the nations of the world.

text:
Republican emails went to spam. Google denies it was political bias. | John Mac Ghlionn, Blaze Media

Who gets to decide which voices reach the American voter?

Every day, Americans send nearly 10 billion emails. Somewhere in that mountain of messages sits a job application, a customer complaint, a school announcement, a bill, or another annoying update from an organization you intended to unsubscribe from five years ago. Most people assume that when they hit send, their message has every chance of reaching its destination. They trust the system to deliver it. That trust deserves scrutiny.

The Republican Party has a $117 million reason to ask questions.

The distinction matters far beyond Republican fundraising.

A new study by researchers at the University of Iowa and the University of Alabama estimates that Republican fundraising lost $117 million in donations during two periods last year, when Gmail’s spam filters actively diverted campaign emails from supporters’ inboxes. Researchers found that first-time donations fell during those periods. They also reported that inbox placement returned to normal after Google stopped using the Spam URI Real-time Blocklist blacklist in September 2025.

Google disputes the study’s methodology, and the research doesn't establish that political bias caused the filtering. But you don't need to be a genius or a tinfoil-hat-wearer to connect the dots. Google's algorithms may be neutral in theory; in practice, however, they have opened up a substantial, and all too predictable, gap in trust. Since the dark days of the Biden years, platform bias is less a conspiracy theory than a documented pattern. Today, elevated skepticism of dismissive claims is hardly unreasonable.

A double-edged sword

Google operates a service used by roughly 90% of the U.S. population. Some 75% of American adults use Gmail. Google’s spam filters perform a necessary job. Nobody wants an inbox packed with fake invoices, phishing attempts, miracle cures, or emails from an incredibly generous Nigerian prince. Spam filtering protects users from fraud and saves them time.

The trouble begins when a system designed to keep garbage out also blocks legitimate messages. A campaign email can disappear into a spam folder without the sender knowing why. The recipient may never realize that a message was sent. Everyone involved can go about their day believing that nothing happened.

That is a remarkable amount of power for a company to exercise through a setting most users never touch.

A government censor has to issue a ban, block a website, or punish a publisher. A technology company, by contrast, can affect what people see through an ordinary technical decision. The message is technically deliverable, yet it may never reach the person expected to receive it.

The distinction matters far beyond Republican fundraising. A small business can spend years building a customer list, only to discover that its emails are reaching fewer people. A charity can ask supporters for donations and wonder why the response has fallen. A local organization can send details of an event that nobody seems to know about.

The sender may blame a bad subject line or a weak appeal. The recipient may assume the sender has gone quiet. The platform sits between them, and neither party necessarily knows what happened.

And a double standard?

For conservatives, the new study raises an obvious concern about political communication. Campaigns depend on supporters receiving updates, invitations, and requests for help. If an email provider’s filtering decisions affect one party’s messages more than another’s, the consequences could reach beyond fundraising.

The same standard must apply to Democrats, Republicans, independents, and organizations with no political affiliation. A free society depends on people being able to communicate with one another. Private companies have a legitimate role in protecting users from scams. But their decisions should be open to meaningful scrutiny when they have major consequences.

With arguably the most consequential midterms in recent history just around the corner, we ought to ask a rather simple question: Who gets to decide which voices reach the American voter?

Google says its protections apply equally to everyone. Users can mark messages as spam. They can block senders or unsubscribe from unwanted emails. Those measures give people some control over what arrives in their inboxes. They offer less help when a legitimate message has already been filtered out.

Google’s new verified-sender program for political campaigns and political action committees raises another question. The program allows participating senders to reach inboxes at a higher rate if they meet Google’s policies. Sender verification can help protect users from impersonation and fraud. That is a reasonable goal.

The public still deserves to know how the program works. People also deserve to know what standards govern participation and whether the same rules apply consistently. Verifying a sender and giving that sender preferential access to an audience are very different things. Users should be able to understand the distinction.

Every reader has a stake in this matter. Email carries information that can affect daily life. A missed job offer can cost someone an opportunity. A filtered school announcement can leave a parent scrambling. A misplaced medical appointment reminder can create an expensive headache. Nobody wants to have to explain to a doctor that Gmail ate the appointment.

The $117 million estimate is a symptom of a broader issue. A handful of ridiculously powerful, notoriously deceptive companies control important routes through which Americans communicate and conduct business.

That power calls for transparency and a meaningful way to challenge unjustified decisions. Conservatives who believe in competition and individual choice have a particular reason to question a system in which so many people depend on a few private gatekeepers.

Americans can hit send whenever they like. The more important question is whether the intended recipient will ever see what they sent.

text:
Look to the stars at the Adler Planetarium in Chicago, Illinois, one of the nation’s most important centers for astronomy and space science. Opened in 1930 on the shore of Lake Michigan, the Adler was the first planetarium in the Western Hemisphere and has introduced generations of visitors to the wonders of the universe.

Inside, visitors can explore exhibits on planets, stars, telescopes, space exploration, and the history of astronomy, then experience immersive shows that bring the night sky and distant worlds to life. Outside, the planetarium’s location on Chicago’s Museum Campus offers some of the most spectacular views of the city skyline and Lake Michigan.

Little-known fact: The Adler’s collection includes rare astronomical instruments dating back centuries, including astrolabes, sundials, and early telescopes that reveal how people studied the heavens long before satellites and spacecraft.

Make it a stop on your next visit to Chicago. Whether you’re fascinated by space, traveling with kids, or simply looking for one of the city’s most memorable museum experiences, the Adler offers a chance to explore the universe without ever leaving the lakefront.

text:
The rain beat steadily against the high arched windows of the lecture hall at the International Defense and Ethics Academy. Inside, two men sat across from one another at a heavy oak table, a stack of operational maps and tactical manuals between them.

Captain David Vance was a twenty-year veteran of a major U.S. metropolitan SWAT team. Across from him sat Commander Yair, a veteran urban combat instructor from the Israel Defense Forces. They had been brought together for a seminar on the evolution of urban engagement, but the conversation had quickly turned to the fundamental philosophy of force.

David leaned forward, tapping a finger on a incident report from Minnesota. "I want you to look at this, Yair. A barricaded suspect, heavy rifles, and seven kids inside the house. My guys took fire the second they breached the perimeter. They were hit, bleeding out in the yard. But they didn't return indiscriminate fire through the walls. They didn't drop a payload on the roof. They accepted the immediate, terrifying risk to their own lives because the presence of those seven children completely vetoed any option that involved overwhelming firepower. That is sacrifice. The mission isn't just neutralizing the threat; it’s preserving the innocent, even if it costs us our own."

Yair looked at the report, his face etched with the exhaustion of a man who had spent years in a very different kind of fight. He slid a satellite map of a dense Gaza neighborhood across the table.

"I respect that bravery, David. Truly," Yair said softly. "But you are describing a domestic crime scene. Look at this map. This isn't one house with one isolated gunman. This is an entire city block where every third basement is connected to a tunnel network, where doorways are rigged with tripwires, and where anti-tank missiles are fired from bedroom windows. When my soldiers advance down these alleys, they aren't facing a criminal; they are facing a heavily armed, dug-in military force. If I send an infantry squad into an un-cleared building without suppressive fire or structural breaches, I am ordering them into a meat grinder. A sovereign military’s first duty under our doctrine is to protect its nation and its own soldiers from destruction."

"I understand the tactical nightmare, Yair," David replied, his voice calm but firm. "Our SWAT teams look at your environment and see the ultimate challenge. But here is the lesson our doctrine offers: the moment a military decides that the tactical risk to its own soldiers justifies flattening an entire residential block—knowing children are inside—the line between military necessity and indiscriminate destruction begins to blur."

David traced his finger over the Gaza map. "In our world, we call it backstop awareness. You never pull the trigger unless you know what is behind your target. If you don't have a clean shot, you hold, you maneuver, or you take the hit. When a military uses heavy aerial bombardment on densely populated civilian areas, the 'backstop' is a family, a school, or a hospital. The rationale is that the enemy is using them as shields, and legally, international law places blame on the force hiding among civilians. But ethically, if your response kills everyone in the house to get the one guy inside, the concept of proportionality is lost."

Yair stared at the map, silent for a moment. "We issue evacuation warnings. We drop leaflets. We tell them to leave."

"And when they have nowhere safe to go?" David countered gently. "That’s where the SWAT mindset can offer a shift in perspective. It’s about shifting from an operational model of contain-and-demolish to one of isolate-and-extract. It means accepting that modern urban warfare cannot be won from 10,000 feet without losing your moral authority. It means investing heavily in specialized, slow, and highly dangerous ground operations—using armored columns, precision close-quarters tactics, and advanced technological intelligence—to surgically remove the threat while physically shielding the non-combatants."

David closed the manual. "It is the hardest way to fight. It increases the risk to the soldier. But true heroism in an urban center isn't measured by how efficiently you can eliminate a target. It is measured by the restraint you show when the target is surrounded by the innocent. If a domestic police officer can lay down his life to save seven children he doesn't know, a modern military must find a way to value the lives of innocent children on the other side of a border, even in the darkest theater of war."

Yair looked from the SWAT report back to the satellite imagery, the silence between the two strategists heavy with the weight of an unresolved, global dilemma.

The Blood of Dawnwalker: How to Unlock Arbiter’s Blade and Obtain St. Mihai’s Legendary Sword

I unlocked Arbiter’s Blade after fighting through Xanthe’s camp and the final ritual against enemies marked with red skulls. It can be done, but if you attempt this quest chain before your character is ready, expect some long fights. I learned that the hard way :D

The most important thing to understand is that having the blacksmith repair St. Mihai’s sword is only part of the process. You still need to complete a separate tempering ritual to obtain the Legendary Imbued Sword of St. Mihai and unlock the achievement.

This guide follows the route I used: Anca’s quests, Albertus, the cathedral caretaker Radu, the repaired stained-glass window, Mihai’s crypt, the three blade shards, and finally the blacksmith and ritual.

It also explains an alternative cathedral route for players who can no longer start the caretaker investigation.

Spoiler warning: this walkthrough reveals quest outcomes, the caretaker’s identity, and the encounter inside Mihai’s crypt.

What you need to restore the sword

There are four components to collect:

• The Broken Sword of St. Mihai, obtained after defeating Mihai in the cathedral crypt. This supplies the surviving section of the weapon, including its hilt.
• One Sword Shard from Forge It Anew: Do Not Disturb.
• One Sword Shard from Forge It Anew: Hostile Takeover.
• One Sword Shard from Forge It Anew: Executive Order.

You can collect the shards in a different order, including before obtaining the broken sword. The order below follows my route and keeps the quest chain easy to follow.

Some investigations and quest interactions advance time. Check the cost shown by the game before confirming them, particularly if you are also working towards rescuing Coen’s family within the time limit.

1. Complete Echoes of Silenced Bells with Anca

Begin by meeting Anca at the old inn near St. Tyna’s. The location is the Crossroads Inn, which is also where you will return for the next quest.

Track Echoes of Silenced Bells in your journal and travel with her to St. Tyna’s Convent in St. Tyna’s Grove. Continue through the opening encounters until you reach the area overlooking the convent courtyard.

The main obstacle here is getting Anca safely to the library. The undead nuns in the courtyard revive, so repeatedly fighting them will not permanently clear the route.

There are different ways to solve this section.

One option is to help Brencis’s soldiers retrieve the Relic of St. Tyna. They are trapped in the infirmary, the courtyard building with the smoking chimney. You can speak to them through an opening around the back.

The relic is in the sacristy on the western side of the courtyard, identifiable by the small cross on its roof. Obtain the Monastery Keys from the wooden shed beside it, enter the sacristy, and retrieve the relic. Giving it to the soldiers gets you the key needed to open the corridor to the library.

Another option uses the convent bells. For this approach, come at night so you can use Coen’s vampiric traversal abilities.

Using the Monastery Keys, enter the building beside the sacristy and read Campana Loquitur, the book describing the nuns’ bell-directed routine. Then reach the bell tower on the eastern side of the courtyard.

Ring the infirmary signal first, followed by the church signal. This sends the nuns against the soldiers and then moves them away from the courtyard.

Once you have secured access, return to Anca and tell her the way to the library is clear. Inside the library, move the bookcase concealing the entrance to the catacombs. Explore below, collect the forbidden books, and defeat Leonica.

At the end, you must decide what to do with Leonica’s ritual notes.

In my playthrough, I burned the notes. Anca survived, and I continued her quest chain.

However, giving her the notes does not kill her or prevent you from obtaining Mihai’s sword. She completes the ritual and frees the cursed nuns. Burning the notes leaves the nuns cursed.

Both choices allow Between the Words to continue, and neither choice prevents a later romance with Anca. You do not need to burn the notes to preserve access to the sword quest.

2. Reveal the hidden text in Between the Words

Return to Anca at the Crossroads Inn and speak to her about studying the forbidden books.

You can prepare a warm drink for her as an optional interaction. Developing your relationship with Anca is separate from the requirements for obtaining the sword; a romance is not necessary.

Examine the books during the study sequence. One volume appears to have blank pages. Bring it to Anca and use the candle to reveal the hidden writing.

The important discovery is the information about St. Mihai and his sword. This gives you the lead that starts A Monk and a Saint and sends you to Albertus.

Before leaving, check your journal. Your next objective should direct you to the monk in the Middens outside Svartrau.

3. Find Albertus in the Middens

The Middens are the largely abandoned district immediately west of Svartrau. In the Polish version, this area is called Szczątki.

Travel into the district and look for writing on the walls. Use Focus Mode to help identify the scribbles, then follow the trail to the house covered in writing.

The markings are a more useful guide than a simple instruction to turn left or right, because your approach depends on which entrance you use.

During my visits, I encountered wolves at night and bandits in the morning. Be prepared for enemies while searching the district.

Inside the house, speak to Albertus about St. Mihai’s sword. Continue the conversation until you can pick up the charcoal and help complete his writing.

Choose the responses in this order:

1. “Abelard the Sorrowful.”
2. “Svartrau Plaza.”
3. “…his penance, the place of his redemption.”
4. “…never once set foot inside it.”
5. The answer beginning “St. Mihai, a great warrior…” and describing his arrival in Vale Sangora.

Completing the conversation points you towards the crypt beneath Svartrau Cathedral.

At this stage, you need to establish two things: where the crypt entrance is hidden, and how to recognise St. Mihai’s symbol.

4. Speak to the Deacon and investigate Radu

Svartrau Cathedral is on the eastern side of the city. The Silberstein shrine is a useful fast-travel point for approaching the cathedral complex.

For the route described here, enter the cathedral during the daytime and speak to the Deacon about the crypt. Agree to find Radu, the missing caretaker, in exchange for access to the cathedral library.

This starts A Dubious Gift.

Important: start this investigation before discovering the crypt’s location through another route. Investigating the well through Night Terrors or finding the cathedral clues independently can make the Deacon’s quest unavailable. Maximum Infamy can also prevent this daytime route.

If you have already lost access to it, use the alternative night route described below. Missing A Dubious Gift does not mean you have lost the sword achievement.

For the caretaker investigation, go to the almshouse north of the main cathedral, within the cathedral complex.

Head upstairs and find Stefan. Speak to him and clean his wound when offered the option. He provides information about the abandoned wing.

Another source of information is the Asylum Resident downstairs, who offers information about Radu for 100 coins.

On the upper floor, search the small rooms for a bookcase with scratch marks on the floor beside it. Activate Focus Mode, inspect the marks, and then move the bookcase.

This reveals the concealed entrance to the abandoned wing.

Follow the passage and stairs down into the basement. At the bottom, you will encounter the Almshouse Monstrosity: Radu, transformed into a monster.

Defeat him and loot the Caretaker’s Key.

You can investigate the abandoned wing further for additional story information, but the key is the essential item for the stained-glass route.

5. Repair the stained glass and read the cathedral records

Use the Caretaker’s Key to open Radu’s shed in the cathedral complex.

Search inside and collect the broken stained-glass pieces. Take them to the craftsman in the cathedral and ask him to reconstruct the window. The repair costs 50 denarii.

The restored image reveals St. Mihai’s symbol: a set of scales.

Remember that symbol. It is the most reliable way to identify the correct memorial stone later.

Return to the Deacon and report what happened to Radu. Completing the investigation grants access to the cathedral library.

Enter the library and search the upper floor for the Annals of the Cathedral. Take the book from its shelf and read it at the nearby reading stand.

The records explain that the entrance to Mihai’s crypt is concealed beneath his memorial stone in the courtyard.

Once you have both pieces of information, the scales symbol and the location beneath the memorial stone, you are ready to find the entrance.

Alternative: discover the crypt at night

If the Deacon’s investigation is unavailable, you can obtain the necessary clues through the nighttime cathedral route.

Approach the cathedral at night and use the exterior scaffolding and Shadowstep to reach the upper interior. Inspect the fresco associated with St. Mihai to learn his symbol.

Remain on the upper platforms while investigating. Xanthe can be present below, and dropping into her path can trigger a separate, difficult encounter.

Outside, investigate the howling from the courtyard well to start Night Terrors. Remove the cover, descend, and examine the body and its letter below.

That investigation provides the clue about the crypt beneath St. Mihai’s memorial stone. Clear the enemies and find the passage out of the well area.

You can then return to the memorial stones and continue with the same crypt encounter.

6. Open Mihai’s crypt and obtain the broken sword

Go to the memorial stones in the courtyard beside the cathedral and almshouse.

The stone I used was the second from the right. More importantly, it bears the scales symbol you learned from the stained glass or another cathedral clue.

Clear away the leaves, inspect the symbol, and move the correct stone to expose the entrance.

I returned at night in my playthrough, but entering the crypt itself is also possible during the day. Nighttime is required for the specific nighttime investigation route, rather than for every possible approach to Mihai.

Descend into the crypt and explore until you find the damaged wall leading into Mihai’s chamber.

Prepare for the fight before breaking through it. Opening the chamber leads to the encounter with Mihai.

Watch for his unblockable attacks, especially the lunges that close the distance quickly. Dodge those attacks rather than trying to block them.

When fog fills the arena, concentrate on defending against his sudden attacks and responding when you have a clear opening. Avoid committing to a long attack sequence while he is disappearing into the mist.

After defeating him, collect the Broken Sword of St. Mihai.

Also search his chamber and inspect the note in his coffin. Reading it is a documented way to start Forge It Anew if you have not already begun the quest by finding a sword component.

Before leaving, check your inventory and journal. You should have the broken sword, and the restoration quest should be available.

7. First Sword Shard: Forge It Anew: Do Not Disturb

The first shard is in a kobold cave in the northeastern part of the Maragir Wealds.

Use the Upper Maragir Wealds shrine as your starting point. The cave is northeast of the shrine, across the river, in the wooded area.

Look for the trail leading towards the kobold den. Investigating this area starts the Do Not Disturb branch of Forge It Anew.

Fight the kobolds outside the entrance, then continue inside and deal with the remaining enemies.

Search the back of the cave for the broken stone cross. Examine it and collect the Sword Shard associated with it.

Before leaving, inspect the painted map or cave markings. These provide leads to the other shard locations and help turn the remaining search into tracked objectives.

This was the easiest shard location for me.

Do not leave after killing the kobolds without examining the cross. Clearing the cave and actually collecting the shard are separate steps.

8. Second Sword Shard: Forge It Anew: Hostile Takeover

For this shard, start from the Giant’s Pawns shrine.

The cave is southwest of the shrine, in the northern part of the Rockfalls region. It is also southwest of Parlita.

Look for a low cave entrance marked with a white X. You will need to crouch to get inside. If the surrounding cliffs make the approach confusing, look for access through the forest on the eastern side.

Inside, you will encounter Munch-Munch, the large corrupted kobold known as Żuj-Żuj in Polish.

This is a tougher fight than the ordinary kobolds at the first location. His attacks can inflict poison, so be prepared to manage both the immediate damage and its lingering effect.

Pay attention to his attack rhythm and make use of the openings after his attacks rather than trying to force damage continuously.

After defeating him, search the nest at the back of the chamber and collect the second Sword Shard.

Inspect the cave’s painted map as well if you have not already obtained all the other location clues.

9. Third Sword Shard: Forge It Anew: Executive Order

This branch begins at another kobold den, but the shard is no longer there when you arrive.

Start at the Crossroads Inn shrine, the same location used for Anca’s book-reading quest.

Head south from the shrine. Take the road branching left and uphill towards the den southeast of the inn, in the southern part of St. Tyna’s Grove.

Enter the den and investigate the nest and nearby clues.

You will discover that Xanthe’s soldiers have already taken the shard. Continue the investigation until your objective directs you to their camp.

Follow that new objective west towards the soldier encampment near Tantari. The camp I visited was southwest of the Drunken Bear Inn.

The inn is a useful landmark, but track Executive Order and use its updated objective to identify the correct camp.

Defeat the soldiers and search the main tent.

The shard is inside a small chest in the tent, on a barrel to the right as you enter.

Collect it and check that the Executive Order branch has advanced or completed.

This was the hardest shard for me to obtain. I fought the camp’s enemies while they were marked with red skulls, and the encounter took a long time.

It is possible, but good timing with dodges and defensive actions matters. If the soldiers are overwhelming you, return after improving your character and equipment.

The empty kobold den is part of this quest’s intended investigation. Once you have found the clue about the soldiers, continue to their camp rather than repeatedly searching the den for the missing shard.

10. Find the Uriashi blacksmith and restore the sword

With the broken sword and all three shards collected, travel to the Uriashi Hermitage in the northwestern part of the Briar Sloughs.

The hermitage lies near the northwestern edge of the world map. Approach through the woodland and continue uphill towards the shrine and clearing.

Look for the lone hornless Uriashi near the large standing stone.

This is the blacksmith who can restore Mihai’s sword. Uriashi describes her people; it is not her personal name.

Speak to her and make it clear that you intend to kill Brencis. Discuss the silver sword and hand over the collected components.

In the route described here, all four components are brought together before the reforge: the Broken Sword of St. Mihai and the three Sword Shards.

Once she has restored the weapon, you will have its Epic version.

Listen to the rest of her explanation and check your journal. The sword still needs to be tempered at an ancient site nearby.

The reforge is an intermediate step. Continue with her instructions to obtain the Legendary version and finish the achievement.

11. Complete the tempering ritual against Echoing Anger

From the Uriashi Hermitage, travel uphill and northwest towards the ancient ruins indicated by the quest.

Look for a cave entrance blocked by red, corrupted vines. With the restored sword, use the interaction to cut through the growth and enter.

Fight through the undead inside the cavern. Continue through the ruins, climb to the higher section, and pass through the doorway leading to the ritual chamber.

The destination is an altar with a glowing red orb above it.

Prepare before interacting with the altar. Activating the ritual begins the Echoing Anger encounter.

This encounter involves successive waves of spectral enemies rather than a straightforward duel with one opponent. Deal with the summoned warriors and wolves until the encounter is complete.

I also fought this section against enemies marked with red skulls. As with Xanthe’s camp, it was possible, but it required patience and a longer fight.

After defeating the final wave, return to the altar and interact with the glowing red orb again.

That second interaction completes the tempering process. Coen imbues the blade during the resulting sequence, restoring its full power.

The finished weapon is the Imbued Sword of St. Mihai, a Legendary Greatsword.

Completing the ritual also unlocks Arbiter’s Blade.

Before you leave, verify the result in your inventory and achievement list. The weapon should now be the Legendary Imbued Sword, and Forge It Anew should be complete.

Quick checks if you are stuck

• Anca’s notes: burning them is not required to keep her alive or continue the sword route. Both choices allow Between the Words to proceed.
• Albertus: pick up the charcoal and complete his writing to obtain the cathedral lead.
• The Deacon: speak to him during the day before independently discovering the crypt. If his investigation is unavailable, use the nighttime route.
• The memorial stone: identify the scales symbol, rather than relying only on the position of the stone.
• The first cave: inspect the broken cross and collect the shard after defeating the kobolds.
• Executive Order: investigate the emptied den, then recover the shard from Xanthe’s camp.
• The blacksmith: three blade shards alone do not replace the Broken Sword of St. Mihai from the crypt.
• The final ritual: return to the altar after the enemy waves. The last interaction is what completes the restoration.

That is the full route I used to obtain the sword. The toughest parts for me were Xanthe’s camp and the final ritual, especially with red-skull enemies, but neither stopped me from finishing the quest.

This is when I unlocked Arbiter’s Blade.

text:
🇵🇭 AFTER HOURS CITY REVIEW: SUBIC BAY, PHILIPPINES

Subic Bay’s after-hours scene remains active heading into 2026, particularly around Barrio Barretto and Olongapo. Recent reports are mixed. Some veterans appreciate its slower pace and old-school atmosphere, while others say the nightlife has declined considerably.

🌙 THE SCENE

Barrio Barretto remains the nightlife hub, although many bars are reportedly quiet during the week. Friday and Saturday are your best bets.

Frequently mentioned venues:

• Queen Victoria - Live music and female company
• Alaska Bar Complex - Among the livelier spots
• Red Bar - Positive reports
• Cloud 69 - Positive reports
• Hotzone - Mixed reviews
• Maze Complex - Reportedly declining
• Barcelona Sports Bar - Relaxed atmosphere

Queen Victoria received conflicting reviews. One November visitor reported several exceptionally attractive women, while others found the selection disappointing.

👠 WOMEN & FREELANCERS

Angeles has a substantially larger adult nightlife scene. One frequent visitor estimated ten times as many women in its bars.

However, Subic regulars describe the women as more relaxed and less demanding.

Freelancers are another option, including women traveling into Subic from elsewhere in Zambales. Olongapo also offers conventional nightlife and opportunities to meet locals.

The takeaway: Fewer options than Angeles, but occasional pleasant surprises.

🏖️ WHERE TO STAY

Barrio Barretto: Best for nightlife and restaurants.

Baloy Beach: Quieter waterfront setting.

Olongapo: More local atmosphere and nightlife.

The main drawback is the busy highway running through Barrio Barretto’s entertainment district.

🏨 HOTELS

Wild Orchid, The Pub Hotel and Central Park Reef are frequently mentioned.

Wild Orchid reportedly has seen better days, while The Pub Hotel received positive feedback. Confirm guest policies before booking.

🍗 FOOD

Food is one of Subic’s strengths. Recommended names include Sparrow’s, Wild Herbs, Johansson’s and Barcelona Sports Bar.

Even visitors disappointed by the nightlife generally praised the dining options.

🌴 BEACHES & ATMOSPHERE

Subic’s coastal location is its biggest advantage over landlocked Angeles, although beaches receive poor reviews due to dirty water and reported sewage runoff.

Some recommend boat trips to nearby islands for swimming and snorkeling.

The atmosphere is older and quieter, with an established Western expatriate community and less Korean influence on the nightlife.

Some appreciate its old-school character. Others find it stagnant and cliquey.

📉 IS SUBIC DECLINING?

Veterans remember a livelier destination. Recent reports describe quiet bars, aging properties and inconsistent nightlife.

However, others still report enjoyable experiences, particularly at Queen Victoria and through independent social connections.

One November visitor initially thought Barrio Barretto looked deserted but left pleasantly surprised.

🔥 BOTTOM LINE

Angeles wins on nightlife variety and consistency. Subic offers a slower pace, coastal setting and smaller bar scene.

For a first visit, book two nights, preferably Friday and Saturday. Stay in Barrio Barretto and explore Queen Victoria and the Alaska complex.

Subic isn’t worth building an entire nightlife holiday around, but it’s a worthwhile short escape from Angeles.

The old Subic hasn’t completely disappeared. You just have to work harder to find it.
